surfaces.*.silentReply.help: Overrides silent-reply policy for one resolved delivery surface. Unset fields inherit agents.defaults.silentReply; use narrow surface ids so internal or group-specific behavior does not spill into other destinations.

diagnostics.enabled.label: Diagnostics Enabled
diagnostics.enabled.help: Master toggle for diagnostics instrumentation output in logs and telemetry wiring paths. Defaults to enabled; set false only in tightly constrained environments.

diagnostics.flags.label: Diagnostics Flags
diagnostics.flags.help: Enable targeted diagnostics logs by flag (e.g. ["telegram.http"]). Supports wildcards like "telegram.*" or "*".

diagnostics.otel.enabled.label: OpenTelemetry Enabled
diagnostics.otel.enabled.help: Enables OpenTelemetry export pipeline for traces, metrics, and logs based on configured endpoint/protocol settings. Keep disabled unless your collector endpoint and auth are fully configured.

diagnostics.otel.endpoint.label: OpenTelemetry Endpoint
diagnostics.otel.endpoint.help: Collector endpoint URL used for OpenTelemetry export transport, including scheme and port. Use a reachable, trusted collector endpoint and monitor ingestion errors after rollout.

diagnostics.otel.tracesEndpoint.label: OpenTelemetry Traces Endpoint
diagnostics.otel.tracesEndpoint.help: Signal-specific OTLP/HTTP trace endpoint. When set, this overrides diagnostics.otel.endpoint and OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT for trace export only.

diagnostics.otel.metricsEndpoint.label: OpenTelemetry Metrics Endpoint
diagnostics.otel.metricsEndpoint.help: Signal-specific OTLP/HTTP metrics endpoint. When set, this overrides diagnostics.otel.endpoint and OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT for metrics export only.

diagnostics.otel.logsEndpoint.label: OpenTelemetry Logs Endpoint
diagnostics.otel.logsEndpoint.help: Signal-specific OTLP/HTTP logs endpoint. When set, this overrides diagnostics.otel.endpoint and OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT for log export only.

diagnostics.otel.protocol.label: OpenTelemetry Protocol
diagnostics.otel.protocol.help: OTel transport protocol for telemetry export. Only "http/protobuf" is accepted; run "openclaw doctor --fix" to repair a persisted legacy "grpc" value or get source-specific manual-edit guidance.

diagnostics.otel.headers.label: OpenTelemetry Headers
diagnostics.otel.headers.help: Additional HTTP request headers sent with OpenTelemetry export requests, often used for tenant auth or routing. Keep secrets in env-backed values and avoid unnecessary header sprawl.

diagnostics.otel.serviceName.label: OpenTelemetry Service Name
diagnostics.otel.serviceName.help: Service name reported in telemetry resource attributes to identify this gateway instance in observability backends. Use stable names so dashboards and alerts remain consistent over deployments.

diagnostics.otel.metricNamePrefix.label: OpenTelemetry Metric Name Prefix
diagnostics.otel.metricNamePrefix.help: Replaces the default "openclaw." prefix on OpenClaw-owned metric names. Use an empty string to remove the prefix, or up to 128 ASCII letters, digits, underscores, dots, hyphens, and slashes starting with a letter. Include any separator you need, for example "acme."; standard gen_ai.* metric names are unchanged. Changing this value requires updating dashboards and alerts that query the old names.

diagnostics.otel.traces.label: OpenTelemetry Traces Enabled
diagnostics.otel.traces.help: Enable trace signal export to the configured OpenTelemetry collector endpoint. Keep enabled when latency/debug tracing is needed, and disable if you only want metrics/logs.

diagnostics.otel.metrics.label: OpenTelemetry Metrics Enabled
diagnostics.otel.metrics.help: Enable metrics signal export to the configured OpenTelemetry collector endpoint. Keep enabled for runtime health dashboards, and disable only if metric volume must be minimized.

diagnostics.otel.logs.label: OpenTelemetry Logs Enabled
diagnostics.otel.logs.help: Enable log signal export through OpenTelemetry in addition to local logging sinks. Use this when centralized log correlation is required across services and agents.

diagnostics.otel.logsExporter.label: OpenTelemetry Logs Exporter
diagnostics.otel.logsExporter.help: Log export sink for diagnostics.otel.logs. Use "otlp" for the configured OTLP logs endpoint, "stdout" for one JSON record per stdout line in container log pipelines, and "both" when both sinks are required.

diagnostics.otel.sampleRate.label: OpenTelemetry Trace Sample Rate
diagnostics.otel.sampleRate.help: Trace sampling rate (0-1) controlling how much trace traffic is exported to observability backends. Lower rates reduce overhead/cost, while higher rates improve debugging fidelity.

diagnostics.otel.flushIntervalMs.label: OpenTelemetry Flush Interval (ms)
diagnostics.otel.flushIntervalMs.help: Interval in milliseconds for periodic telemetry flush from buffers to the collector. Increase to reduce export chatter, or lower for faster visibility during active incident response.

diagnostics.otel.captureContent.label: OpenTelemetry Content Capture
diagnostics.otel.captureContent.help: Opt-in OTEL span content capture. Defaults to off; true captures non-system message and tool content.

diagnostics.cacheTrace.enabled.label: Cache Trace Enabled
diagnostics.cacheTrace.enabled.help: Log cache trace snapshots for embedded agent runs (default: false).

agents.entries.*.identity.avatar.label: Identity Avatar
agents.entries.*.identity.avatar.help: Agent avatar (workspace-relative path, http(s) URL, or data URI).

agents.entries.*.skills.label: Agent Skill Filter
agents.entries.*.skills.help: Optional allowlist of skills for this agent. If omitted, the agent inherits agents.defaults.skills when set; otherwise skills stay unrestricted. Set [] for no skills. An explicit list fully replaces inherited defaults instead of merging with them.

agents.entries.*.cwd.label: Agent Working Directory
agents.entries.*.cwd.help: Working directory for this agent's reply runs. Overrides agents.defaults.cwd but not session-spawned cwd; bootstrap and memory files stay in workspace. Supports ~ and relative paths; a distinct cwd requires an unsandboxed run.

agents.entries.*.runtime.label: Agent Runtime
agents.entries.*.runtime.help: Optional runtime descriptor for this agent. Use embedded for default OpenClaw execution or acp for external ACP harness defaults.

agents.entries.*.runtime.type.label: Agent Runtime Type
agents.entries.*.runtime.type.help: Runtime type for this agent: "embedded" (default OpenClaw runtime) or "acp" (ACP harness defaults).

agents.entries.*.runtime.acp.label: Agent ACP Runtime
agents.entries.*.runtime.acp.help: ACP runtime defaults for this agent when runtime.type=acp. Binding-level ACP overrides still take precedence per conversation.

agents.entries.*.runtime.acp.agent.label: Agent ACP Harness Agent
agents.entries.*.runtime.acp.agent.help: Optional ACP harness agent id to use for this OpenClaw agent (for example codex, claude, cursor, gemini, openclaw).

agents.entries.*.runtime.acp.backend.label: Agent ACP Backend
agents.entries.*.runtime.acp.backend.help: Optional ACP backend override for this agent's ACP sessions (falls back to global acp.backend).

agents.entries.*.runtime.acp.mode.label: Agent ACP Mode
agents.entries.*.runtime.acp.mode.help: Optional ACP session mode default for this agent (persistent or oneshot).

agents.entries.*.runtime.acp.cwd.label: Agent ACP Working Directory
agents.entries.*.runtime.acp.cwd.help: Optional default working directory for this agent's ACP sessions.

agents.entries.*.thinkingDefault.label: Agent Thinking Default
agents.entries.*.thinkingDefault.help: Optional per-agent default thinking level. Overrides agents.defaults.thinkingDefault for this agent when no per-message or session override is set.

agents.entries.*.reasoningDefault.label: Agent Reasoning Default
agents.entries.*.reasoningDefault.help: Optional per-agent default reasoning visibility (on|off|stream). Applies when no per-message or session reasoning override is set.

agents.entries.*.fastModeDefault.label: Agent Fast Mode Default
agents.entries.*.fastModeDefault.help: Optional per-agent default for fast mode ("auto", true, or false). Applies when no per-message or session fast-mode override is set.

agents.defaults.fastModeDefault.label: Default Agent Fast Mode
agents.defaults.fastModeDefault.help: Default fast-mode policy for the agent loop ("auto", true, or false). Individual agent entries override it.

agents.entries.*.contextInjection.label: Agent Context Injection
agents.entries.*.contextInjection.help: Per-agent override for when workspace bootstrap files are injected into this agent's system prompt. Omit to inherit agents.defaults.contextInjection.

agents.entries.*.bootstrapMaxChars.label: Agent Bootstrap Max Chars
agents.entries.*.bootstrapMaxChars.help: Per-agent override for max characters of each workspace bootstrap file injected into this agent's system prompt. Omit to inherit agents.defaults.bootstrapMaxChars.

agents.entries.*.bootstrapTotalMaxChars.label: Agent Bootstrap Total Max Chars
agents.entries.*.bootstrapTotalMaxChars.help: Per-agent override for max total characters across all workspace bootstrap files injected into this agent's system prompt. Omit to inherit agents.defaults.bootstrapTotalMaxChars.

agents.entries.*.experimental.label: Agent Experimental Flags
agents.entries.*.experimental.help: Per-agent experimental flags. Omitted fields inherit agents.defaults.experimental.

agents.entries.*.experimental.localModel.label: Agent Lean Local Model Mode
agents.entries.*.experimental.localModel.help: Per-agent override for lean local-model mode. Enable it for one smaller local-model agent without trimming tools from every agent.

agents.ownership.label: Agent Ownership Generation
agents.ownership.help: Durable multi-agent ownership generation marker. "explicit" means ambient channels, heartbeat, system-agent consults, Talk, cron, and bare CLI operations must resolve a surface-specific owner or fail closed. OpenClaw stamps this automatically when creating or migrating a fleet; omit it for a sole agent.

agents.defaults.label: Agent Defaults
agents.defaults.help: Shared default settings inherited by agents unless overridden per entry in agents.entries. Use defaults to enforce consistent baseline behavior and reduce duplicated per-agent configuration.

agents.defaults.contextLimits.label: Default Context Limits
agents.defaults.contextLimits.help: Focused per-agent-context budget defaults for selected high-volume excerpts and injected prompt blocks. Use this to tune bounded read/injection sizes without reopening any unbounded call paths.

agents.defaults.contextLimits.memoryGetM.label: Default memory_get Max Chars
agents.defaults.contextLimits.memoryGetM.help: Default max characters returned by memory_get before truncation metadata and continuation notice are added. Increase to approximate older larger excerpts, but keep it bounded.

agents.defaults.contextLimits.postCompac.label: Default Post-compaction Max Chars
agents.defaults.contextLimits.postCompac.help: Default max characters retained from AGENTS.md during post-compaction context refresh injection. Lower this to make compaction recovery cheaper, or raise it for agents that depend on longer startup guidance.

agents.entries.label: Agent List
agents.entries.help: Explicit list of configured agents with IDs and optional overrides for model, tools, identity, and workspace. Keep IDs stable over time so bindings, approvals, and session routing remain deterministic.

agents.entries.*.skillsLimits.label: Agent Skills Limits
agents.entries.*.skillsLimits.help: Optional per-agent overrides for skills subsystem budgets. Use this when an agent needs a different skills prompt budget without introducing a second generic context-limits path.

agents.entries.*.skillsLimits.maxSkillsP.label: Agent Skills Prompt Max Chars
agents.entries.*.skillsLimits.maxSkillsP.help: Per-agent override for the skills prompt character budget. This extends the existing skills.limits.maxSkillsPromptChars path instead of routing the same budget through contextLimits.

agents.entries.*.contextLimits.label: Agent Context Limits
agents.entries.*.contextLimits.help: Optional per-agent overrides for the focused context budget knobs. Omitted fields inherit agents.defaults.contextLimits.

agents.entries.*.contextLimits.memoryGet.label: Agent memory_get Max Chars
agents.entries.*.contextLimits.memoryGet.help: Per-agent override for the default memory_get max character budget.

agents.entries.*.contextLimits.postCompa.label: Agent Post-compaction Max Chars
agents.entries.*.contextLimits.postCompa.help: Per-agent override for the post-compaction AGENTS.md excerpt budget.

agents.entries.*.models.label: Agent Model Overrides
agents.entries.*.models.help: Per-agent model catalog overrides keyed by full provider/model IDs.

agents.entries.*.modelPolicy.label: Agent Model Policy
agents.entries.*.modelPolicy.help: Per-agent model override policy. An explicit allow list replaces the default policy for this agent.

agents.entries.*.modelPolicy.allow.label: Allowed Agent Models
agents.entries.*.modelPolicy.allow.help: Allowed model override refs for this agent. Accepts aliases, full "provider/model" refs, and trailing prefix wildcards such as "provider/*" or "provider/namespace/*"; empty permits any model.

agents.entries.*.models.*.agentRuntime.label: Agent Model Runtime
agents.entries.*.models.*.agentRuntime.help: Optional per-model runtime policy for this agent. Use this for agent-specific model exceptions instead of setting a whole-agent runtime.

agents.entries.*.models.*.agentRuntime.i.label: Agent Model Runtime ID
agents.entries.*.models.*.agentRuntime.i.help: Per-agent model runtime id: "openclaw", "auto", a registered plugin harness id such as "codex", or a supported CLI backend alias such as "claude-cli".

agents.entries.*.models.*.codeMode.label: Code Mode
agents.entries.*.models.*.codeMode.help: OpenClaw Code Mode for this agent and exact provider/model: On forces it on, Off disables it, and Default inherits the agent activation setting, then the shared model override, then tools.codeMode.enabled. This does not change the selected runtime or Codex native Code Mode.

cloudWorkers.desktop.label: Cloud Worker Desktop (Labs)
cloudWorkers.desktop.help: Enables the experimental worker.desktop.observe surface and Control UI Desktop panel for desktop-capable cloud worker environments.

cloudWorkers.projectProfiles.label: Cloud Worker Project Profiles
cloudWorkers.projectProfiles.help: Default cloud worker profile names keyed by normalized lowercase repository identity (host/owner/repo). Explicit dispatch profile ids take precedence.

cloudWorkers.projectProfiles.*.label: Cloud Worker Project Profile
cloudWorkers.projectProfiles.*.help: Cloud worker profile name used by default when a session worktree's origin matches this repository identity.

cloudWorkers.profiles.label: Cloud Worker Profiles
cloudWorkers.profiles.help: Named cloud worker profiles. Each profile selects a worker provider registered by a plugin and carries provider-owned settings.

cloudWorkers.profiles.*.label: Cloud Worker Profile
cloudWorkers.profiles.*.help: One cloud worker profile selected by name when creating an environment. Keep provider credentials in supported references rather than embedding secret material in this block.

cloudWorkers.profiles.*.provider.label: Cloud Worker Provider
cloudWorkers.profiles.*.provider.help: Worker provider id registered by a plugin. The configured plugin must expose this id before the gateway can provision environments from the profile.

cloudWorkers.profiles.*.install.label: Cloud Worker Install Method
cloudWorkers.profiles.*.install.help: Worker installation method: "bundle" (default) transfers the gateway's content-hashed installed build and supports released, development, and unreleased versions; "npm" installs the exact gateway version and is available only when that version is released.

cloudWorkers.profiles.*.suspendAfter.label: Cloud Worker Idle Suspend Duration
cloudWorkers.profiles.*.suspendAfter.help: Automatically reclaims an idle cloud worker after this duration, such as 45m or 2h; the next message provisions a replacement. Minimum: 1m. Leave unset to keep workers running.

cloudWorkers.profiles.*.settings.label: Cloud Worker Provider Settings
cloudWorkers.profiles.*.settings.help: Provider-owned settings validated by the selected plugin. Use SecretRef objects for secret-bearing values; opaque settings do not gain automatic secret resolution.

desktop.host.label: Gateway Host Desktop
desktop.host.help: Experimental gateway-host desktop observation backed by an existing or managed loopback VNC server.

desktop.host.enabled.label: Gateway Host Desktop (Labs)
desktop.host.enabled.help: Enables the experimental gateway-host desktop source. Restart the gateway after changing this setting.

desktop.host.managed.label: Managed Linux Host Desktop
desktop.host.managed.help: Runs and supervises a loopback-only headless TigerVNC/XFCE desktop on Linux. An explicit port or existing default-port VNC server still takes precedence.

desktop.host.port.label: Gateway Host VNC Port
desktop.host.port.help: Loopback RFB port of an already-running VNC server on the gateway host (default: 5900).

desktop.host.passwordFile.label: Gateway Host VNC Password File
desktop.host.passwordFile.help: Absolute path to the VNC password file. Omit on macOS to use account/ARD authentication after that support lands.

gateway.port.label: Gateway Port
gateway.port.help: TCP port used by the gateway listener for API, control UI, and channel-facing ingress paths. Use a dedicated port and avoid collisions with reverse proxies or local developer services.

gateway.mode.label: Gateway Mode
gateway.mode.help: Gateway operation mode: "local" runs channels and agent runtime on this host, while "remote" connects through remote transport. Keep "local" unless you intentionally run a split remote gateway topology.

gateway.bind.label: Gateway Bind Mode
gateway.bind.help: Network bind profile: "auto", "lan", "loopback", "custom", or "tailnet" to control interface exposure. Keep "loopback" for local-only operation; "auto" can expose all interfaces.

gateway.customBindHost.label: Gateway Custom Bind Host
gateway.customBindHost.help: IPv4 address used for a custom bind. Specific IPv4s also require the same Gateway port on 127.0.0.1; avoid 0.0.0.0 unless all-interface exposure is required.

gateway.publicOrigin.label: Gateway Public Origin
gateway.publicOrigin.help: Externally reachable HTTPS origin of the Gateway. HTTP is allowed only for localhost, 127.0.0.1, or [::1]. Per-requester MCP OAuth uses it to build the callback URL at /oauth/mcp/callback; channel session links and plugin-generated viewer links use it to reach the Control UI and Gateway routes.

gateway.controlUi.label: Control UI
gateway.controlUi.help: Control UI hosting settings including enablement, pathing, and browser-origin/auth hardening behavior. Keep UI exposure minimal and pair with strong auth controls before internet-facing deployments.

gateway.controlUi.enabled.label: Control UI Enabled
gateway.controlUi.enabled.help: Enables serving the gateway Control UI from the gateway HTTP process when true. Keep enabled for local administration, and disable when an external control surface replaces it.

gateway.cliAgents.label: CLI Agents
gateway.cliAgents.help: Experimental Control UI discovery for external CLI session engines exposed by the Gateway session catalog. Enabled by default; disable to prevent starting those engines from the new-session model picker.

gateway.cliAgents.enabled.label: CLI Agents Enabled
gateway.cliAgents.enabled.help: Shows catalog-backed CLI agents in the Control UI new-session model picker when true (default: true). Set false to disable CLI agents and native CLI session creation. Only catalogs that advertise session creation are listed, and the picker stays hidden when the Gateway does not advertise session catalog support.

gateway.terminal.label: Operator Terminal
gateway.terminal.help: Operator terminal served to Control UI and mobile clients: a PTY-backed shell on the gateway host, restricted to admin-scope operator sessions. It starts in the target agent's workspace and is refused for fully-sandboxed agents (sandbox.mode 'all') rather than handing back an unconfined host shell.

gateway.terminal.enabled.label: Operator Terminal Enabled
gateway.terminal.enabled.help: Enables the operator terminal for admin-scope clients (default: true). This exposes a browser/mobile shell with the gateway process environment; set false to opt out on deployments where admin operators should not get a host shell. Changing this restarts the gateway so connected clients reload with the correct terminal availability and content-security policy.

gateway.terminal.shell.label: Operator Terminal Shell
gateway.terminal.shell.help: Shell executable the operator terminal launches. Leave unset to use the host login shell ($SHELL on Unix, %ComSpec% on Windows), or pin an explicit interpreter for a consistent operator environment.

gateway.terminal.detachedSessionTimeoutS.label: Operator Terminal Detached Session Timeout
gateway.terminal.detachedSessionTimeoutS.help: Seconds a terminal session survives after its connection drops (laptop sleep, page reload), staying reattachable via terminal.attach with its recent output replayed. Set 0 to kill sessions the moment the connection drops. Default: 300 (5 minutes). Detached sessions keep running their commands, so shorten this on shared or exposed hosts.

gateway.auth.label: Gateway Auth
gateway.auth.help: Authentication policy for gateway HTTP/WebSocket access including mode, credentials, trusted-proxy behavior, and rate limiting. Keep auth enabled for every non-loopback deployment.

gateway.auth.mode.label: Gateway Auth Mode
gateway.auth.mode.help: Gateway auth mode: "none", "token", "password", or "trusted-proxy" depending on your edge architecture. Token/password mode selects the configured secret (gateway.auth.token or gateway.auth.password); clients may send it in either connect auth field. Use token/password for direct exposure, and trusted-proxy only behind hardened identity-aware proxies.

gateway.auth.allowTailscale.label: Gateway Auth Allow Tailscale Identity
gateway.auth.allowTailscale.help: Allows trusted Tailscale identity paths to satisfy gateway auth checks when configured. Use this only when your tailnet identity posture is strong and operator workflows depend on it.

gateway.auth.identityScopes.label: Gateway Identity Scope Grants
gateway.auth.identityScopes.help: Maps verified trusted-proxy or Tailscale identities to connection-only operator scope grants. Email keys match case-insensitively; grants augment device scopes before the connection scope cap is applied.

gateway.auth.rateLimit.label: Gateway Auth Rate Limit
gateway.auth.rateLimit.help: Login/auth attempt throttling controls to reduce credential brute-force risk at the gateway boundary. Keep enabled in exposed environments and tune thresholds to your traffic baseline.

gateway.auth.trustedProxy.label: Gateway Trusted Proxy Auth
gateway.auth.trustedProxy.help: Trusted-proxy auth header mapping for upstream identity providers that inject user claims. Use only with known proxy CIDRs and strict header allowlists to prevent spoofed identity headers.

gateway.auth.trustedProxy.deviceAutoAppr.label: Trusted Proxy Device Auto-Approval
gateway.auth.trustedProxy.deviceAutoAppr.help: Optional policy for automatically approving new browser and native UI operator devices and same-key scope upgrades after trusted-proxy authentication. Grants are capped by deviceAutoApprove.scopes and the proxy's x-openclaw-scopes header when present.

gateway.auth.trustedProxy.deviceAutoAppr.label: Trusted Proxy Device Auto-Approval Enabled
gateway.auth.trustedProxy.deviceAutoAppr.help: Automatically approves new browser and native UI operator devices and same-key scope upgrades after the reverse proxy authenticates an allowed user. Default: false. Enable only when the proxy identity boundary is strong enough to replace manual device pairing.

gateway.auth.trustedProxy.deviceAutoAppr.label: Trusted Proxy Device Auto-Approval Scopes
gateway.auth.trustedProxy.deviceAutoAppr.help: Maximum scopes granted to auto-approved operator devices. Defaults to operator.read, operator.write, operator.approvals, and operator.questions. Requested scopes are capped to this list; requests without scopes receive this list. When unset, auto-approval also adds operator.questions for older UI clients; an explicit list is never widened. Explicitly listing operator.admin lets every proxy-authenticated user auto-approve full admin and makes scope-less requests receive full admin automatically; it also triggers a critical security audit finding and Gateway startup warning.

gateway.roles.label: Gateway Operator Roles
gateway.roles.help: Optional profile-bound operator roles for team Gateways. Each named role controls access to other people's sessions, sandbox isolation, session and run agents, and granted operator scopes; omitting this section preserves existing operator behavior.

gateway.roles.default.label: Default Operator Role
gateway.roles.default.help: Required role assigned to authenticated profiles without a valid explicit assignment whenever operator roles are configured. Its name must match a configured role definition.

gateway.roles.definitions.label: Operator Role Definitions
gateway.roles.definitions.help: Nonempty administrator-named role definitions bundling the closed session-sharing, sandbox-isolation, agent-access, and operator-scope policies applied to authenticated user profiles.

gateway.roles.definitions.*.label: Operator Role Definition
gateway.roles.definitions.*.help: One named operator role. Every definition must explicitly provide its session-sharing policy, allowed session and run agents, and operator-scope ceiling, and can require sandbox isolation for newly created sessions.

gateway.roles.definitions.*.sessions.label: Operator Role Session Access
gateway.roles.definitions.*.sessions.help: Session-sharing permissions granted to this role for sessions created by other authenticated people; a person's own sessions remain owner-accessible.

gateway.roles.definitions.*.sessions.oth.label: Operator Role Access to Other Sessions
gateway.roles.definitions.*.sessions.oth.help: Access to other people's sessions: "none" hides them, "view" allows reading, "suggest" permits the suggestion flow, and "write" permits participation. Explicit session membership can grant additional access.

gateway.roles.definitions.*.sandbox.label: Operator Role Sandbox Isolation
gateway.roles.definitions.*.sandbox.help: Execution isolation for newly created sessions: "inherit" (default) uses the agent policy; "required" permanently requires a sandbox, even when the agent sandbox mode is off, and fails closed if the backend is unavailable.

gateway.roles.definitions.*.agents.label: Operator Role Allowed Agents
gateway.roles.definitions.*.agents.help: Agents available when this role creates sessions or starts runs: set "*" to allow every agent, list agent IDs to allow only those agents, or use an empty list to disable both.

gateway.roles.definitions.*.scopes.label: Operator Role Scope Ceiling
gateway.roles.definitions.*.scopes.help: Closed list of operator scopes granted as this role's maximum connection authority. Requested, paired, identity-granted, and upgraded scopes are intersected with this list.

gateway.trustedProxies.label: Gateway Trusted Proxy CIDRs
gateway.trustedProxies.help: CIDR/IP allowlist of upstream proxies permitted to provide forwarded client identity headers. Keep this list narrow so untrusted hops cannot impersonate users.

gateway.allowRealIpFallback.label: Gateway Allow x-real-ip Fallback
gateway.allowRealIpFallback.help: Enables x-real-ip fallback when x-forwarded-for is missing in proxy scenarios. Keep disabled unless your ingress stack requires this compatibility behavior.

gateway.tools.label: Gateway Tool Exposure Policy
gateway.tools.help: Gateway-level tool exposure allow/deny policy that can restrict runtime tool availability independent of agent/tool profiles. Use this for coarse emergency controls and production hardening.

gateway.tools.allow.label: Gateway Tool Allowlist
gateway.tools.allow.help: Explicit gateway-level tool allowlist when you want a narrow set of tools available at runtime. Use this for locked-down environments where tool scope must be tightly controlled.

gateway.tools.deny.label: Gateway Tool Denylist
gateway.tools.deny.help: Explicit gateway-level tool denylist to block risky tools even if lower-level policies allow them. Use deny rules for emergency response and defense-in-depth hardening.

gateway.tailscale.label: Gateway Tailscale
gateway.tailscale.help: Tailscale integration settings for Serve/Funnel exposure and lifecycle handling on gateway start/exit. Keep off unless your deployment intentionally relies on Tailscale ingress.

gateway.tailscale.mode.label: Gateway Tailscale Mode
gateway.tailscale.mode.help: Tailscale publish mode: "off", "serve", or "funnel" for private or public exposure paths. Use "serve" for tailnet-only access and "funnel" only when public internet reachability is required.

gateway.tailscale.preserveFunnel.label: Gateway Tailscale External Funnel Migration Guard
gateway.tailscale.preserveFunnel.help: Deprecated migration guard for mode='serve'. If an external Funnel still targets the ordinary Gateway listener, OpenClaw leaves exposure unchanged and warns that only plugin-authenticated webhooks remain usable until password auth is configured and mode is migrated to 'funnel'.

gateway.remote.label: Remote Gateway
gateway.remote.help: Remote gateway connection settings for direct or SSH transport when this instance proxies to another runtime host. Use remote mode only when split-host operation is intentionally configured.

gateway.remote.transport.label: Remote Gateway Transport
gateway.remote.transport.help: Remote connection transport: "direct" uses configured URL connectivity, while "ssh" tunnels through SSH. Use SSH when you need encrypted tunnel semantics without exposing remote ports.

gateway.reload.label: Config Reload
gateway.reload.help: Live config-reload policy for how edits are applied and when full restarts are triggered. Keep hybrid behavior for safest operational updates unless debugging reload internals.

gateway.tls.label: Gateway TLS
gateway.tls.help: TLS certificate and key settings for terminating HTTPS directly in the gateway process. Use explicit certificates in production and avoid plaintext exposure on untrusted networks.

gateway.tls.enabled.label: Gateway TLS Enabled
gateway.tls.enabled.help: Enables TLS termination at the gateway listener so clients connect over HTTPS/WSS directly. Keep enabled for direct internet exposure or any untrusted network boundary.

gateway.tls.autoGenerate.label: Gateway TLS Auto-Generate Cert
gateway.tls.autoGenerate.help: Auto-generates a local TLS certificate/key pair when explicit files are not configured. Use only for local/dev setups and replace with real certificates for production traffic.

gateway.tls.certPath.label: Gateway TLS Certificate Path
gateway.tls.certPath.help: Filesystem path to the TLS certificate file used by the gateway when TLS is enabled. Use managed certificate paths and keep renewal automation aligned with this location.

gateway.tls.keyPath.label: Gateway TLS Key Path
gateway.tls.keyPath.help: Filesystem path to the TLS private key file used by the gateway when TLS is enabled. Keep this key file permission-restricted and rotate per your security policy.

gateway.tls.caPath.label: Gateway TLS CA Path
gateway.tls.caPath.help: Optional CA bundle path for client verification or custom trust-chain requirements at the gateway edge. Use this when private PKI or custom certificate chains are part of deployment.

gateway.http.label: Gateway HTTP API
gateway.http.help: Gateway HTTP API configuration grouping endpoint toggles and transport-facing API exposure controls. Keep only required endpoints enabled to reduce attack surface.

gateway.http.endpoints.label: Gateway HTTP Endpoints
gateway.http.endpoints.help: HTTP endpoint feature toggles under the gateway API surface for compatibility routes and optional integrations. Enable endpoints intentionally and monitor access patterns after rollout.

gateway.http.securityHeaders.label: Gateway HTTP Security Headers
gateway.http.securityHeaders.help: Optional HTTP response security headers applied by the gateway process itself. Prefer setting these at your reverse proxy when TLS terminates there.

gateway.http.securityHeaders.strictTrans.label: Strict Transport Security Header
gateway.http.securityHeaders.strictTrans.help: Value for the Strict-Transport-Security response header. Set only on HTTPS origins that you fully control; use false to explicitly disable.

gateway.remote.url.label: Remote Gateway URL
gateway.remote.url.help: Remote Gateway WebSocket URL (ws:// or wss://).

gateway.remote.sshTarget.label: Remote Gateway SSH Target
gateway.remote.sshTarget.help: Remote gateway over SSH (tunnels the gateway port to localhost). Format: user@host or user@host:port.

gateway.remote.sshIdentity.label: Remote Gateway SSH Identity
gateway.remote.sshIdentity.help: Optional SSH identity file path (passed to ssh -i).

gateway.remote.sshHostKeyPolicy.label: Remote Gateway SSH Host-Key Policy
gateway.remote.sshHostKeyPolicy.help: macOS SSH host-key verification policy. "strict" requires an already trusted host key; "openssh" explicitly delegates to effective OpenSSH configuration.

gateway.remote.token.label: Remote Gateway Token
gateway.remote.token.help: Shared secret sent in the token field to authenticate this client to a remote gateway. The server's gateway.auth.mode selects its configured secret; either client token or password field is accepted. Store via secret/env substitution and rotate alongside remote gateway auth changes.

gateway.remote.password.label: Remote Gateway Password
gateway.remote.password.help: Shared secret sent in the password field to authenticate this client to a remote gateway. The server's gateway.auth.mode selects its configured secret; either client token or password field is accepted. Keep this secret managed externally and avoid plaintext values in committed config.

gateway.remote.edgeAuth.label: Remote Gateway Edge Auth Headers
gateway.remote.edgeAuth.help: Secret-backed HTTP headers presented to an identity-aware proxy in front of the configured remote Gateway. Headers are sent only to the exact gateway.remote.url origin over WSS and never follow redirects.

gateway.remote.tlsFingerprint.label: Remote Gateway TLS Fingerprint
gateway.remote.tlsFingerprint.help: Expected sha256 TLS fingerprint for the remote gateway (pin to avoid MITM).

gateway.auth.token.label: Gateway Token
gateway.auth.token.help: Shared secret selected by gateway.auth.mode=token, the default for new local onboarding. Clients may send it in either auth.token or auth.password. Non-loopback binds require an enabled authentication mode.

gateway.auth.password.label: Gateway Password
gateway.auth.password.help: Shared secret selected by gateway.auth.mode=password. Clients may send it in either auth.token or auth.password. Password mode is required for Tailscale Funnel.

browser.enabled.label: Browser Enabled
browser.enabled.help: Enables browser capability wiring in the gateway so browser tools and CDP-driven workflows can run. Disable when browser automation is not needed to reduce surface area and startup work.

browser.allowSystemProfileImport.label: Allow System Profile Import
browser.allowSystemProfileImport.help: Allows macOS hosts to import cookies from a local Chrome-family system profile into a managed OpenClaw browser profile. Disable this to prevent browser profile cookie import and its macOS Keychain consent prompt.

browser.cdpUrl.label: Browser CDP URL
browser.cdpUrl.help: CDP/DevTools endpoint URL used to attach to an externally managed browser instance. Use this for centralized browser hosts, tunnels, or existing-session attachment, and keep URL access restricted to trusted network paths.

browser.executablePath.label: Browser Executable Path
browser.executablePath.help: Explicit browser executable path when auto-discovery is insufficient for your host environment. Use an absolute stable path, or a path starting with ~ for your OS home directory, so launch behavior stays deterministic across restarts.

browser.headless.label: Browser Headless Mode
browser.headless.help: Forces browser launch in headless mode when the local launcher starts browser instances. Keep headless enabled for server environments and disable only when visible UI debugging is required.

browser.noSandbox.label: Browser No-Sandbox Mode
browser.noSandbox.help: Disables Chromium sandbox isolation flags for environments where sandboxing fails at runtime. Keep this off whenever possible because process isolation protections are reduced.

browser.attachOnly.label: Browser Attach-only Mode
browser.attachOnly.help: Restricts browser mode to attach-only behavior without starting local browser processes. Use this when all browser sessions are externally managed by a remote CDP provider.

browser.defaultProfile.label: Browser Default Profile
browser.defaultProfile.help: Default browser profile name selected when callers do not explicitly choose a profile. Use a stable low-privilege profile as the default to reduce accidental cross-context state use.

browser.profiles.label: Browser Profiles
browser.profiles.help: Named browser profile connection map used for explicit routing to CDP ports or URLs with optional metadata. Keep profile names consistent and avoid overlapping endpoint definitions.

browser.profiles.*.cdpPort.label: Browser Profile CDP Port
browser.profiles.*.cdpPort.help: Per-profile local CDP port used when connecting to browser instances by port instead of URL. Use unique ports per profile to avoid connection collisions.

browser.profiles.*.cdpUrl.label: Browser Profile CDP URL
browser.profiles.*.cdpUrl.help: Per-profile CDP/DevTools endpoint URL used for explicit browser routing by profile name. Use this for remote CDP hosts, tunnels, or existing-session profiles that should attach through a running Chrome DevTools endpoint.

browser.profiles.*.userDataDir.label: Browser Profile User Data Dir
browser.profiles.*.userDataDir.help: Per-profile Chromium user data directory for existing-session attachment through Chrome DevTools MCP. Use this for Brave, Edge, Chromium, or non-default Chrome profiles when the built-in auto-connect path would pick the wrong browser data directory on the selected host or browser node. Paths starting with ~ expand to the OS home directory.

browser.profiles.*.mcpCommand.label: Browser Profile Chrome MCP Command
browser.profiles.*.mcpCommand.help: Per-profile Chrome DevTools MCP command for existing-session attachment. Defaults to npx.

browser.profiles.*.mcpArgs.label: Browser Profile Chrome MCP Args
browser.profiles.*.mcpArgs.help: Extra per-profile Chrome DevTools MCP arguments for existing-session attachment, such as --no-usage-statistics. Endpoint arguments here override the built-in auto-connect or browser URL selection.

browser.profiles.*.driver.label: Browser Profile Driver
browser.profiles.*.driver.help: Per-profile browser driver mode. Use "openclaw" (or legacy "clawd") for CDP-based profiles, "existing-session" for Chrome DevTools MCP attachment, or "extension" for the authenticated Chrome extension relay.

browser.profiles.*.executablePath.label: Browser Profile Executable Path
browser.profiles.*.executablePath.help: Per-profile browser executable path for locally launched managed browser profiles. Overrides browser.executablePath and accepts paths starting with ~ for the OS home directory.

browser.profiles.*.headless.label: Browser Profile Headless Mode
browser.profiles.*.headless.help: Per-profile headless override for locally launched browser instances. Use this when one profile should stay headless without forcing browser.headless for every other profile.

browser.profiles.*.attachOnly.label: Browser Profile Attach-only Mode
browser.profiles.*.attachOnly.help: Per-profile attach-only override that skips local browser launch and only attaches to an existing CDP endpoint. Useful when one profile is externally managed but others are locally launched.

browser.extensionRelay.label: Browser Extension Relay
browser.extensionRelay.help: Chrome extension relay authentication compatibility settings. Keep the legacy window only while older paired extensions or external CDP clients still need it.

browser.extensionRelay.allowLegacyAuth.label: Allow Legacy Browser Relay Auth
browser.extensionRelay.allowLegacyAuth.help: Temporarily accepts legacy Bearer, Basic, and token-subprotocol relay authentication. Default: true for one migration window. Set false after every extension and external CDP client uses Browser Relay Authentication v2.

tools.allow.label: Tool Allowlist
tools.allow.help: Absolute tool allowlist that replaces profile-derived defaults for strict environments. Use this only when you intentionally run a tightly curated subset of tool capabilities.

tools.deny.label: Tool Denylist
tools.deny.help: Global tool denylist that blocks listed tools even when profile or provider rules would allow them. Use deny rules for emergency lockouts and long-term defense-in-depth.

tools.web.label: Web Tools
tools.web.help: Web-tool policy grouping for search/fetch providers, limits, and fallback behavior tuning. Keep enabled settings aligned with API key availability and outbound networking policy.

tools.exec.label: Exec Tool
tools.exec.help: Exec-tool policy grouping for shell execution host, security mode, approval behavior, and runtime bindings. Keep conservative defaults in production and tighten elevated execution paths.

tools.github.label: GitHub CLI Identity and Git Author
tools.github.help: Managed local GitHub CLI profile and optional Git author for agent tools. Omit this object to preserve the Gateway runtime user's native account and author; repository remote credentials are never overridden.

tools.github.profileId.label: GitHub Profile Version
tools.github.profileId.help: Opaque generated profile version used to switch managed credentials atomically.

tools.github.kind.label: GitHub Credential Kind
tools.github.kind.help: Marks a managed OAuth profile whose rotating refresh credential is owned by the Gateway. Omitted profiles use a personal access token.

tools.github.gitAuthor.name.label: Git Author Name
tools.github.gitAuthor.name.help: Optional process-local Git author and committer name.

tools.github.gitAuthor.email.label: Git Author Email
tools.github.gitAuthor.email.help: Optional process-local Git author and committer email.

agents.entries.*.tools.github.label: Agent GitHub CLI Identity Override
agents.entries.*.tools.github.help: Complete managed GitHub CLI identity and Git author override for this agent. Omit it to inherit the system identity.

tools.media.image.enabled.label: Enable Image Understanding
tools.media.image.enabled.help: Enable image understanding so attached or referenced images can be interpreted into textual context. Disable if you need text-only operation or want to avoid image-processing cost.

tools.media.image.preferredModel.label: Preferred Image Understanding Model
tools.media.image.preferredModel.help: Prefer one capability-tagged tools.media.models entry for image understanding before the remaining compatible fallbacks.

tools.media.image.maxBytes.label: Image Understanding Max Bytes
tools.media.image.maxBytes.help: Default image input size limit for configured and auto-detected models. Set this to match provider payload limits and deployment bandwidth.

tools.media.image.maxChars.label: Image Understanding Max Chars
tools.media.image.maxChars.help: Default maximum image description length. Use a lower value for compact context or a higher value for detailed OCR and scene analysis.

tools.media.image.prompt.label: Image Understanding Prompt
tools.media.image.prompt.help: Default image-understanding prompt when an entry does not override it. Keep this deterministic when consumers rely on stable descriptions.

tools.media.image.timeoutSeconds.label: Image Understanding Timeout (sec)
tools.media.image.timeoutSeconds.help: Default timeout for image-understanding requests. Increase it for large images or slower local vision models.

tools.media.image.scope.label: Image Understanding Scope
tools.media.image.scope.help: Restrict image understanding by channel, chat type, or source key. Keep this narrow in busy or untrusted channels to control processing.

tools.media.image.attachments.label: Image Understanding Attachment Policy
tools.media.image.attachments.help: Choose which matching image attachments are processed. Use first-only handling unless multi-image analysis is intentional.

tools.media.models.label: Media Understanding Shared Models
tools.media.models.help: Canonical media-understanding model list. Use image, audio, or video capability tags on every entry so each pipeline selects only compatible fallbacks.

tools.media.concurrency.label: Media Understanding Concurrency
tools.media.concurrency.help: Maximum number of concurrent media understanding operations per turn across image, audio, and video tasks. Lower this in resource-constrained deployments to prevent CPU/network saturation.

tools.media.audio.enabled.label: Enable Audio Understanding
tools.media.audio.enabled.help: Enable audio understanding so voice notes or audio clips can be transcribed for agent context.

tools.media.audio.preferredModel.label: Preferred Audio Understanding Model
tools.media.audio.preferredModel.help: Prefer one capability-tagged tools.media.models entry for audio transcription before the remaining compatible fallbacks.

tools.media.audio.maxBytes.label: Audio Understanding Max Bytes
tools.media.audio.maxBytes.help: Default audio input size limit for configured and auto-detected models. Set this to the largest recording your providers and network should accept.

tools.media.audio.maxChars.label: Audio Understanding Max Chars
tools.media.audio.maxChars.help: Default maximum transcript length for configured and auto-detected models. Use a lower value to keep long voice notes from expanding agent context.

tools.media.audio.prompt.label: Audio Understanding Prompt
tools.media.audio.prompt.help: Default audio transcription prompt when a model entry does not override it. Keep the instruction stable when downstream workflows rely on transcript style.

tools.media.audio.timeoutSeconds.label: Audio Understanding Timeout (sec)
tools.media.audio.timeoutSeconds.help: Default timeout for audio understanding requests. Increase it for long recordings or slower local transcription models.

tools.media.audio.language.label: Audio Understanding Language
tools.media.audio.language.help: Default language hint for audio transcription providers. Set it when the primary spoken language is known and provider detection is unreliable.

tools.media.audio.scope.label: Audio Understanding Scope
tools.media.audio.scope.help: Restrict audio understanding by channel, chat type, or source key. Keep this narrow where automatic transcription is sensitive or expensive.

tools.media.audio.attachments.label: Audio Understanding Attachment Policy
tools.media.audio.attachments.help: Choose which matching audio attachments are processed. Use first-only handling unless multi-attachment transcription is intentional.

tools.media.audio.echoTranscript.label: Echo Transcript to Chat
tools.media.audio.echoTranscript.help: Echo the audio transcript to the originating chat before agent processing. Enable this when users need to verify what the system heard.

tools.media.audio.echoFormat.label: Transcript Echo Format
tools.media.audio.echoFormat.help: Format the echoed transcript with a {transcript} placeholder. Keep the placeholder intact so delivery includes the transcript.

tools.media.video.enabled.label: Enable Video Understanding
tools.media.video.enabled.help: Enable video understanding so clips can be summarized into text for downstream reasoning and responses. Disable when processing video is out of policy or too expensive for your deployment.

tools.media.video.preferredModel.label: Preferred Video Understanding Model
tools.media.video.preferredModel.help: Prefer one capability-tagged tools.media.models entry for video understanding before the remaining compatible fallbacks.

tools.media.video.maxBytes.label: Video Understanding Max Bytes
tools.media.video.maxBytes.help: Default video input size limit for configured and auto-detected models. Set this to match provider payload limits and deployment bandwidth.

tools.media.video.maxChars.label: Video Understanding Max Chars
tools.media.video.maxChars.help: Default maximum video description length. Use a lower value for compact context or a higher value for detailed scene summaries.

tools.media.video.prompt.label: Video Understanding Prompt
tools.media.video.prompt.help: Default video-understanding prompt when an entry does not override it. Keep this deterministic when consumers rely on stable summaries.

tools.media.video.timeoutSeconds.label: Video Understanding Timeout (sec)
tools.media.video.timeoutSeconds.help: Default timeout for video-understanding requests. Increase it for longer clips or slower local analysis models.

tools.media.video.scope.label: Video Understanding Scope
tools.media.video.scope.help: Restrict video understanding by channel, chat type, or source key. Keep this narrow in busy or untrusted channels to control processing.

tools.media.video.attachments.label: Video Understanding Attachment Policy
tools.media.video.attachments.help: Choose which matching video attachments are processed. Use first-only handling unless multi-video analysis is intentional.

tools.links.enabled.label: Enable Link Understanding
tools.links.enabled.help: Enable automatic link understanding pre-processing so URLs can be summarized before agent reasoning. Keep enabled for richer context, and disable when strict minimal processing is required.

tools.links.maxLinks.label: Link Understanding Max Links
tools.links.maxLinks.help: Maximum number of links expanded per turn during link understanding. Use lower values to control latency/cost in chatty threads and higher values when multi-link context is critical.

tools.links.timeoutSeconds.label: Link Understanding Timeout (sec)
tools.links.timeoutSeconds.help: Per-link understanding timeout budget in seconds before unresolved links are skipped. Keep this bounded to avoid long stalls when external sites are slow or unreachable.

tools.links.models.label: Link Understanding Models
tools.links.models.help: Preferred model list for link understanding tasks, evaluated in order as fallbacks when supported. Use lightweight models first for routine summarization and heavier models only when needed.

tools.links.scope.label: Link Understanding Scope
tools.links.scope.help: Controls when link understanding runs relative to conversation context and message type. Keep scope conservative to avoid unnecessary fetches on messages where links are not actionable.

tools.profile.label: Tool Profile
tools.profile.help: Global tool profile name used to select a predefined tool policy baseline before applying allow/deny overrides. Use this for consistent environment posture across agents and keep profile names stable.

tools.alsoAllow.label: Tool Allowlist Additions
tools.alsoAllow.help: Extra tool allowlist entries merged on top of the selected tool profile and default policy. Keep this list small and explicit so audits can quickly identify intentional policy exceptions.

agents.entries.*.tools.profile.label: Agent Tool Profile
agents.entries.*.tools.profile.help: Per-agent override for tool profile selection when one agent needs a different capability baseline. Use this sparingly so policy differences across agents stay intentional and reviewable.

agents.entries.*.tools.alsoAllow.label: Agent Tool Allowlist Additions
agents.entries.*.tools.alsoAllow.help: Per-agent additive allowlist for tools on top of global and profile policy. Keep narrow to avoid accidental privilege expansion on specialized agents.

agents.entries.*.tools.codeMode.label: Agent Code Mode
agents.entries.*.tools.codeMode.help: Per-agent Code Mode options. Explicit enabled overrides the shared model and global activation defaults; an agent-specific model codeMode override wins. Other options merge over tools.codeMode without changing activation.

agents.entries.*.tools.swarm.label: Agent Swarm
agents.entries.*.tools.swarm.help: Per-agent swarm override. Values merge over the top-level tools.swarm configuration.

tools.byProvider.label: Tool Policy by Provider
tools.byProvider.help: Per-provider tool allow/deny overrides keyed by channel/provider ID to tailor capabilities by surface. Use this when one provider needs stricter controls than global tool policy.

agents.entries.*.tools.byProvider.label: Agent Tool Policy by Provider
agents.entries.*.tools.byProvider.help: Per-agent provider-specific tool policy overrides for channel-scoped capability control. Use this when a single agent needs tighter restrictions on one provider than others.

agents.entries.*.tools.message.crossCont.label: Agent Cross-Context Messaging (Same Provider)
agents.entries.*.tools.message.crossCont.help: Per-agent message guard for sending to other conversations on the same provider. Set false for current-conversation-only public agents.

agents.entries.*.tools.message.crossCont.label: Agent Cross-Context Messaging (Across Providers)
agents.entries.*.tools.message.crossCont.help: Per-agent message guard for sending across providers. Keep false for public or sandboxed agents.

agents.entries.*.tools.message.actions.a.label: Agent Message Action Allowlist
agents.entries.*.tools.message.actions.a.help: Per-agent message action allowlist for the message tool. Set to a minimal list such as ["send"] for public sandbox agents so read, edit, delete, reaction, and other provider-specific message actions stay hidden and blocked.

tools.exec.applyPatch.enabled.label: Enable apply_patch
tools.exec.applyPatch.enabled.help: Enable or disable apply_patch for OpenAI and OpenAI Codex models when allowed by tool policy (default: true).

tools.exec.applyPatch.workspaceOnly.label: apply_patch Workspace-Only
tools.exec.applyPatch.workspaceOnly.help: Restrict apply_patch paths to the workspace directory (default: true). Set false to allow writing outside the workspace (dangerous).

tools.exec.applyPatch.allowModels.label: apply_patch Model Allowlist
tools.exec.applyPatch.allowModels.help: Optional allowlist of model ids (e.g. "gpt-5.4" or "openai/gpt-5.4").

tools.loopDetection.enabled.label: Tool-loop Detection
tools.loopDetection.enabled.help: Enable repetitive tool-call loop detection and backoff safety checks (default: false).

tools.fs.workspaceOnly.label: Workspace-only FS tools
tools.fs.workspaceOnly.help: Restrict filesystem tools (read/write/edit/apply_patch) to the workspace directory (default: false).

tools.sessions.visibility.label: Session Tools Visibility
tools.sessions.visibility.help: Controls which sessions can be targeted by sessions_list/sessions_history/sessions_search/sessions_send/session_status. ("all" default = any session on the Gateway, including other agents and users; "agent" = any session in the current agent id; "self" = only current; "tree" = current session + spawned subagent sessions). Cross-agent access is on by default and scoped by tools.agentToAgent; use narrower visibility to restrict access.

tools.exec.notifyOnExit.label: Exec Notify On Exit
tools.exec.notifyOnExit.help: When true (default), backgrounded exec sessions on exit and node exec lifecycle events enqueue a system event and request a heartbeat.

tools.exec.notifyOnExitEmptySuccess.label: Exec Notify On Empty Success
tools.exec.notifyOnExitEmptySuccess.help: When true, successful backgrounded exec exits with empty output still enqueue a completion system event (default: false).

tools.exec.approvalRunningNoticeMs.label: Exec Approval Running Notice (ms)
tools.exec.approvalRunningNoticeMs.help: Delay in milliseconds before showing an in-progress notice after an exec approval is granted. Increase to reduce flicker for fast commands, or lower for quicker operator feedback.

tools.exec.host.label: Exec Target
tools.exec.host.help: Selects execution target strategy for shell commands. Use "auto" for runtime-aware behavior (sandbox when available, otherwise gateway), or pin sandbox/gateway/node explicitly when you need a fixed surface.

tools.exec.mode.label: Exec Mode
tools.exec.mode.help: Normalized exec policy selector. Use "auto" for classifier-reviewed approval misses, "ask" for human-reviewed misses, "allowlist" for deterministic safe commands only, or "full" for trusted local operation.

tools.exec.reviewer.label: Exec Reviewer
tools.exec.reviewer.help: Model-backed exec reviewer used by auto mode before human approval fallback. Configure a narrow model override here when you want exec review isolated from the main agent model.

tools.exec.reviewer.model.label: Exec Reviewer Model
tools.exec.reviewer.model.help: Optional provider/model override for the exec reviewer agent. Omit to reuse the configured primary model for the target agent.

tools.exec.reviewer.timeoutMs.label: Exec Reviewer Timeout (ms)
tools.exec.reviewer.timeoutMs.help: Per-stage exec reviewer timeout in milliseconds for model preparation and completion before falling back to human approval (default: 30000).

tools.exec.node.label: Exec Node Binding
tools.exec.node.help: Node binding configuration for exec tooling when command execution is delegated through connected nodes. Use explicit node binding only when multi-node routing is required.

tools.agentToAgent.label: Agent-to-Agent Tool Access
tools.agentToAgent.help: Policy for cross-agent session tool calls: sends, list, history, search, and status reads (default: enabled). Use allow to restrict agent pairs; enabled=false blocks ordinary cross-agent access. Requester-owned native subagent and ACP child sessions stay reachable under tree or all visibility. For strict separation, set tools.sessions.visibility to agent or self (tree still admits requester-owned native/ACP children), or use separate gateways.

tools.agentToAgent.enabled.label: Enable Agent-to-Agent Tool
tools.agentToAgent.enabled.help: Enables cross-agent session tool access (default: true); omitted or empty allow permits every agent pair. Set false to block ordinary cross-agent access; requester-owned native subagent and ACP child sessions stay reachable under tree or all visibility. For strict separation, set tools.sessions.visibility to agent or self (tree still admits requester-owned native/ACP children), or use separate gateways.

tools.agentToAgent.allow.label: Agent-to-Agent Target Allowlist
tools.agentToAgent.allow.help: Agent ids or * patterns that may take part in cross-agent calls; the requesting and target agent must both match. Cross-agent access is on by default, and omitted or empty allow permits every pair. Set an explicit list to restrict access; blank entries deny.

tools.updatePlan.label: Enable Structured Plan Tool
tools.updatePlan.help: Unified `progress_card` status tool for durable plans and narrative notes in parent sessions. Enabled by default; set false to opt out. Always unavailable to subagents.

tools.toolSearch.label: Tool Search
tools.toolSearch.help: Compact large OpenClaw, MCP, and client tool catalogs. Supported local runtimes use structured Tool Search automatically when unset. Set false to disable it, true for the code bridge, or use the object form to choose a mode.

tools.toolSearch.enabled.label: Enable Tool Search
tools.toolSearch.enabled.help: Enables Tool Search. When on, OpenClaw hides large tool catalogs behind `tool_search_code` or structured search/describe/call tools during embedded runtime runs.

tools.toolSearch.mode.label: Tool Search Surface
tools.toolSearch.mode.help: Choose the model-facing surface: "code" exposes `tool_search_code`; "tools" exposes structured search/describe/call fallback tools; "directory" keeps a bounded tool directory visible, exposes a bounded set of likely or required schemas, and defers the rest behind search/describe/call.

tools.toolSearch.codeTimeoutMs.label: Tool Search Code Timeout
tools.toolSearch.codeTimeoutMs.help: Maximum milliseconds for one `tool_search_code` execution. Runtime clamps values to the supported 1s..60s range.

tools.toolSearch.searchDefaultLimit.label: Tool Search Default Results
tools.toolSearch.searchDefaultLimit.help: Default number of Tool Search results returned when the model omits a limit. Runtime clamps this to `maxSearchLimit`.

tools.toolSearch.maxSearchLimit.label: Tool Search Max Results
tools.toolSearch.maxSearchLimit.help: Maximum number of Tool Search results a model can request. Runtime clamps values to the supported 1..50 range.

tools.codeMode.label: Code Mode
tools.codeMode.help: Generic OpenClaw code mode. When enabled, agent runs expose only `exec` and `wait` to the model and hide normal tools behind a QuickJS-WASI catalog bridge.

tools.codeMode.enabled.label: Enable Code Mode
tools.codeMode.enabled.help: Global OpenClaw Code Mode default. Off when omitted, including objects without `enabled`. `"auto"` engages catalog-preferred models; `true` engages tool-capable runs. Agent and model activation overrides take precedence. An engaged run fails closed if the runtime is unavailable instead of exposing the full tool list.

tools.codeMode.runtime.label: Code Mode Runtime
tools.codeMode.runtime.help: Guest JavaScript runtime. Only "quickjs-wasi" is supported.

tools.codeMode.mode.label: Code Mode Surface
tools.codeMode.mode.help: Model-facing surface. Only "only" is supported: expose code-mode `exec` and `wait` and hide normal tools.

tools.codeMode.languages.label: Code Mode Languages
tools.codeMode.languages.help: Accepted source languages for `exec`. Supported values are "javascript" and "typescript".

tools.codeMode.timeoutMs.label: Code Mode Timeout
tools.codeMode.timeoutMs.help: Maximum milliseconds for one code-mode `exec` or `wait` call.

tools.codeMode.memoryLimitBytes.label: Code Mode Memory Limit
tools.codeMode.memoryLimitBytes.help: QuickJS heap limit for one code-mode VM.

tools.codeMode.maxOutputBytes.label: Code Mode Output Limit
tools.codeMode.maxOutputBytes.help: Maximum serialized bytes returned through code-mode output.

tools.codeMode.maxSnapshotBytes.label: Code Mode Snapshot Limit
tools.codeMode.maxSnapshotBytes.help: Maximum serialized bytes retained for one suspended QuickJS snapshot.

tools.codeMode.maxPendingToolCalls.label: Code Mode Pending Tool Limit
tools.codeMode.maxPendingToolCalls.help: Maximum concurrent nested tool calls a code-mode VM can start before it must resume later.

tools.codeMode.snapshotTtlSeconds.label: Code Mode Snapshot TTL
tools.codeMode.snapshotTtlSeconds.help: How long suspended code-mode snapshots can be resumed with `wait` before they expire.

tools.codeMode.searchDefaultLimit.label: Code Mode Default Search Results
tools.codeMode.searchDefaultLimit.help: Default number of hidden catalog search results returned by `catalog.search` inside code mode.

tools.codeMode.maxSearchLimit.label: Code Mode Max Search Results
tools.codeMode.maxSearchLimit.help: Maximum number of hidden catalog search results a code-mode program can request.

tools.swarm.label: Swarm
tools.swarm.help: Collector-mode subagent orchestration. Enabled by default; set false to opt out. Tool permissions still apply to agents_wait and swarm spawn options.

tools.swarm.enabled.label: Enable Swarm
tools.swarm.enabled.help: Enables collector-mode subagents and agents_wait. Default is on; set false to opt out.

tools.swarm.maxConcurrent.label: Swarm Concurrent Children
tools.swarm.maxConcurrent.help: Maximum concurrently running collector children per swarm group.

tools.swarm.maxChildrenPerGroup.label: Swarm Live Children per Group
tools.swarm.maxChildrenPerGroup.help: Maximum live collector children per swarm group.

tools.swarm.maxTotalPerGroup.label: Swarm Total Children per Group
tools.swarm.maxTotalPerGroup.help: Maximum lifetime collector spawns per swarm group.

tools.swarm.waitTimeoutSecondsMax.label: Swarm Maximum Wait Timeout
tools.swarm.waitTimeoutSecondsMax.help: Maximum timeout accepted by agents_wait, in seconds.

tools.swarm.defaultAgentId.label: Swarm Default Agent
tools.swarm.defaultAgentId.help: Default target agent for swarm spawns that omit agentId. The subagent allowlist still applies.

tools.elevated.label: Elevated Tool Access
tools.elevated.help: Elevated tool access controls for privileged command surfaces that should only be reachable from trusted senders. Keep disabled unless operator workflows explicitly require elevated actions.

tools.elevated.enabled.label: Enable Elevated Tool Access
tools.elevated.enabled.help: Enables elevated tool execution path when sender and policy checks pass. Keep disabled in public/shared channels and enable only for trusted owner-operated contexts.

tools.elevated.allowFrom.label: Elevated Tool Allow Rules
tools.elevated.allowFrom.help: Sender allow rules for elevated tools, usually keyed by channel/provider identity formats. Use narrow, explicit identities so elevated commands cannot be triggered by unintended users.

tools.subagents.label: Subagent Tool Policy
tools.subagents.help: Tool policy wrapper for spawned subagents to restrict or expand tool availability compared to parent defaults. Use this to keep delegated agent capabilities scoped to task intent.

tools.subagents.tools.label: Subagent Tool Allow/Deny Policy
tools.subagents.tools.help: Allow/deny tool policy applied to spawned subagent runtimes. Keep this narrower than parent scope. Parent-owned tools such as progress_card are always denied, including through allow/alsoAllow.

tools.sandbox.label: Sandbox Tool Policy
tools.sandbox.help: Tool policy wrapper for sandboxed agent executions so sandbox runs can have distinct capability boundaries. Use this to enforce stronger safety in sandbox contexts.

tools.sandbox.tools.label: Sandbox Tool Allow/Deny Policy
tools.sandbox.tools.help: Allow/deny tool policy applied when agents run in sandboxed execution environments. Keep policies minimal so sandbox tasks cannot escalate into unnecessary external actions.

tools.exec.pathPrepend.label: Exec PATH Prepend
tools.exec.pathPrepend.help: Directories to prepend to PATH for exec runs (gateway/sandbox).

tools.exec.safeBins.label: Exec Safe Bins
tools.exec.safeBins.help: Allow stdin-only safe binaries to run without explicit allowlist entries.

tools.exec.strictInlineEval.label: Require Inline-Eval Approval
tools.exec.strictInlineEval.help: Require explicit approval for interpreter inline-eval forms such as `python -c`, `node -e`, `ruby -e`, or `osascript -e`. Prevents silent allowlist reuse and downgrades allow-always to ask-each-time for those forms.

tools.exec.commandHighlighting.label: Exec Command Highlighting
tools.exec.commandHighlighting.help: Show parser-derived command highlights in exec approval prompts (default: false). Enable this to render highlighted command text without changing exec approval policy.

tools.exec.grantExpiryDays.label: Standing Grant Expiry (Days)
tools.exec.grantExpiryDays.help: Default lifetime, in days (1-3650), for standing grants minted by allow-always on automation approvals. Unset keeps grants valid until revoked or the owning automation changes. Terms freeze at mint, so changing this affects only future grants.

tools.exec.safeBinTrustedDirs.label: Exec Safe Bin Trusted Dirs
tools.exec.safeBinTrustedDirs.help: Additional explicit directories trusted for safe-bin path checks (PATH entries are never auto-trusted).

tools.exec.safeBinProfiles.label: Exec Safe Bin Profiles
tools.exec.safeBinProfiles.help: Optional per-binary safe-bin profiles (positional limits + allowed/denied flags).

approvals.exec.label: Exec Approval Forwarding
approvals.exec.help: Groups exec-approval forwarding behavior including enablement, routing mode, filters, and explicit targets. Configure here when approval prompts must reach operational channels instead of only the origin thread.

approvals.exec.enabled.label: Forward Exec Approvals
approvals.exec.enabled.help: Enables forwarding of exec approval requests to configured delivery destinations (default: false). Keep disabled in low-risk setups and enable only when human approval responders need channel-visible prompts.

approvals.exec.mode.label: Approval Forwarding Mode
approvals.exec.mode.help: Controls where approval prompts are sent: "session" uses origin chat, "targets" uses configured targets, and "both" sends to both paths. Use "session" as baseline and expand only when operational workflow requires redundancy.

approvals.exec.agentFilter.label: Approval Agent Filter
approvals.exec.agentFilter.help: Optional allowlist of agent IDs eligible for forwarded approvals, for example `["primary", "ops-agent"]`. Use this to limit forwarding blast radius and avoid notifying channels for unrelated agents.

approvals.exec.sessionFilter.label: Approval Session Filter
approvals.exec.sessionFilter.help: Optional session-key filters matched as substring or regex-style patterns, for example `["discord:", "^agent:ops:"]`. Use narrow patterns so only intended approval contexts are forwarded to shared destinations.

approvals.exec.targets.label: Approval Forwarding Targets
approvals.exec.targets.help: Explicit delivery targets used when forwarding mode includes targets, each with channel and destination details. Keep target lists least-privilege and validate each destination before enabling broad forwarding.

approvals.exec.targets[].channel.label: Approval Target Channel
approvals.exec.targets[].channel.help: Channel/provider ID used for forwarded approval delivery, such as discord, slack, or a plugin channel id. Use valid channel IDs only so approvals do not silently fail due to unknown routes.

approvals.exec.targets[].to.label: Approval Target Destination
approvals.exec.targets[].to.help: Destination identifier inside the target channel (channel ID, user ID, or thread root depending on provider). Verify semantics per provider because destination format differs across channel integrations.

approvals.exec.targets[].accountId.label: Approval Target Account ID
approvals.exec.targets[].accountId.help: Optional account selector for multi-account channel setups when approvals must route through a specific account context. Use this only when the target channel has multiple configured identities.

approvals.exec.targets[].threadId.label: Approval Target Thread ID
approvals.exec.targets[].threadId.help: Optional thread/topic target for channels that support threaded delivery of forwarded approvals. Use this to keep approval traffic contained in operational threads instead of main channels.

approvals.plugin.label: Plugin Approval Forwarding
approvals.plugin.help: Groups plugin-approval forwarding behavior including enablement, routing mode, filters, and explicit targets. Independent of exec approval forwarding. Configure here when plugin approval prompts must reach operational channels.

approvals.plugin.enabled.label: Forward Plugin Approvals
approvals.plugin.enabled.help: Enables forwarding of plugin approval requests to configured delivery destinations (default: false). Independent of approvals.exec.enabled.

approvals.plugin.mode.label: Plugin Approval Forwarding Mode
approvals.plugin.mode.help: Controls where plugin approval prompts are sent: "session" uses origin chat, "targets" uses configured targets, and "both" sends to both paths.

approvals.plugin.agentFilter.label: Plugin Approval Agent Filter
approvals.plugin.agentFilter.help: Optional allowlist of agent IDs eligible for forwarded plugin approvals, for example `["primary", "ops-agent"]`. Use this to limit forwarding blast radius.

approvals.plugin.sessionFilter.label: Plugin Approval Session Filter
approvals.plugin.sessionFilter.help: Optional session-key filters matched as substring or regex-style patterns, for example `["discord:", "^agent:ops:"]`. Use narrow patterns so only intended approval contexts are forwarded.

approvals.plugin.targets.label: Plugin Approval Forwarding Targets
approvals.plugin.targets.help: Explicit delivery targets used when plugin approval forwarding mode includes targets, each with channel and destination details.

approvals.plugin.targets[].channel.label: Plugin Approval Target Channel
approvals.plugin.targets[].channel.help: Channel/provider ID used for forwarded plugin approval delivery, such as discord, slack, or a plugin channel id.

approvals.plugin.targets[].to.label: Plugin Approval Target Destination
approvals.plugin.targets[].to.help: Destination identifier inside the target channel (channel ID, user ID, or thread root depending on provider).

approvals.plugin.targets[].accountId.label: Plugin Approval Target Account ID
approvals.plugin.targets[].accountId.help: Optional account selector for multi-account channel setups when plugin approvals must route through a specific account context.

approvals.plugin.targets[].threadId.label: Plugin Approval Target Thread ID
approvals.plugin.targets[].threadId.help: Optional thread/topic target for channels that support threaded delivery of forwarded plugin approvals.

tools.message.crossContext.allowWithinPr.label: Allow Cross-Context (Same Provider)
tools.message.crossContext.allowWithinPr.help: Allow sends to other channels within the same provider (default: true).

tools.message.crossContext.allowAcrossPr.label: Allow Cross-Context (Across Providers)
tools.message.crossContext.allowAcrossPr.help: Allow sends across different providers (default: false).

tools.message.crossContext.marker.enable.label: Cross-Context Marker
tools.message.crossContext.marker.enable.help: Add a visible origin marker when sending cross-context (default: true).

tools.message.actions.allow.label: Message Action Allowlist
tools.message.actions.allow.help: Global message action allowlist for the message tool. Use only when the whole runtime should expose and accept a reduced action set; prefer per-agent allowlists for public or sandboxed agents.

tools.web.search.enabled.label: Enable Web Search Tool
tools.web.search.enabled.help: Enable managed web_search and optional Codex-native search for eligible models.

tools.web.search.provider.label: Web Search Provider
tools.web.search.provider.help: Search provider id. Auto-detected from available API keys if omitted.

tools.web.search.timeoutSeconds.label: Web Search Timeout (sec)
tools.web.search.timeoutSeconds.help: Timeout in seconds for web_search requests.

tools.web.search.cacheTtlMinutes.label: Web Search Cache TTL (min)
tools.web.search.cacheTtlMinutes.help: Cache TTL in minutes for web_search results.

tools.web.search.openaiCodex.enabled.label: Enable Native Codex Web Search
tools.web.search.openaiCodex.enabled.help: Enable native Codex web search for Codex-capable models.

tools.web.search.openaiCodex.mode.label: Codex Web Search Mode
tools.web.search.openaiCodex.mode.help: Native Codex web search preference: "cached" (default; unrestricted Codex turns resolve it to live) or "live".

tools.web.search.openaiCodex.allowedDoma.label: Codex Allowed Domains
tools.web.search.openaiCodex.allowedDoma.help: Domain allowlist for native Codex web_search. On native-hosted-search turns, it also gates managed web_fetch; managed-provider turns are unchanged.

tools.web.search.openaiCodex.contextSize.label: Codex Search Context Size
tools.web.search.openaiCodex.contextSize.help: Native Codex search context size hint: "low", "medium", or "high".

tools.web.search.openaiCodex.userLocatio.label: Codex User Country
tools.web.search.openaiCodex.userLocatio.help: Approximate country sent to native Codex web search.

tools.web.search.openaiCodex.userLocatio.label: Codex User Region
tools.web.search.openaiCodex.userLocatio.help: Approximate region/state sent to native Codex web search.

tools.web.search.openaiCodex.userLocatio.label: Codex User City
tools.web.search.openaiCodex.userLocatio.help: Approximate city sent to native Codex web search.

tools.web.search.openaiCodex.userLocatio.label: Codex User Timezone
tools.web.search.openaiCodex.userLocatio.help: Approximate timezone sent to native Codex web search.

tools.web.fetch.enabled.label: Enable Web Fetch Tool
tools.web.fetch.enabled.help: Enable the web_fetch tool (lightweight HTTP fetch).

tools.web.fetch.maxCharsCap.label: Web Fetch Hard Max Chars
tools.web.fetch.maxCharsCap.help: Hard cap for web_fetch maxChars (applies to config and tool calls).

tools.web.fetch.timeoutSeconds.label: Web Fetch Timeout (sec)
tools.web.fetch.timeoutSeconds.help: Timeout in seconds for web_fetch requests.

tools.web.fetch.cacheTtlMinutes.label: Web Fetch Cache TTL (min)
tools.web.fetch.cacheTtlMinutes.help: Cache TTL in minutes for web_fetch results.

tools.web.fetch.userAgent.label: Web Fetch User-Agent
tools.web.fetch.userAgent.help: Override User-Agent header for web_fetch requests.

tools.web.fetch.headers.label: Web Fetch Request Headers
tools.web.fetch.headers.help: Extra request headers sent with direct web_fetch requests, for example gateway routing or authentication headers. Every configured value is treated as sensitive and redacted from exposed config and debug captures. Values are plain strings, support ${VAR} substitution and the global $${VAR} literal escape, and are sent to model-chosen URLs. Entries are validated when the request is built rather than at config load, so a bad name or unsendable value is dropped and logged instead of disabling the surface; Accept, Accept-Language, User-Agent, and framing headers such as Transfer-Encoding are dropped too. Use tools.web.fetch.userAgent to change the user agent. Cross-origin redirects retain only the guarded-fetch safe header allowlist, and changing the headers actually sent partitions the fetch cache.

tools.web.fetch.readability.label: Web Fetch Readability Extraction
tools.web.fetch.readability.help: Use Readability to extract main content from HTML (fallbacks to basic HTML cleanup).

tools.web.fetch.useTrustedEnvProxy.label: Web Fetch Trusted Env Proxy
tools.web.fetch.useTrustedEnvProxy.help: Route web_fetch through a trusted HTTP(S) env proxy and let the proxy resolve DNS. Enable only when that proxy is operator-controlled and enforces outbound policy after DNS resolution.

tools.web.fetch.ssrfPolicy.label: Web Fetch SSRF Policy
tools.web.fetch.ssrfPolicy.help: Scoped SSRF policy overrides for web_fetch. Keep this narrow and opt in only for known local-network proxy environments.

tools.web.fetch.ssrfPolicy.dangerouslyAl.label: Web Fetch Dangerously Allow Private Network
tools.web.fetch.ssrfPolicy.dangerouslyAl.help: Allows web_fetch access to private and internal network targets. Keep disabled unless model-selected URLs are trusted in this deployment.

tools.web.fetch.ssrfPolicy.allowedHostna.label: Web Fetch Allowed Hostnames
tools.web.fetch.ssrfPolicy.allowedHostna.help: Exact hostnames or IP literals allowed for web_fetch, including otherwise blocked targets. Keep the list minimal.

tools.web.fetch.ssrfPolicy.blockedHostna.label: Web Fetch Blocked Hostnames
