commands.bashForegroundMs.label: Bash Foreground Window (ms)
commands.bashForegroundMs.help: How long bash waits before backgrounding (default: 2000; 0 backgrounds immediately).

commands.config.label: Allow /config
commands.config.help: Allow /config chat command to read/write config on disk (default: false).

commands.mcp.label: Allow /mcp
commands.mcp.help: Allow /mcp chat command to manage OpenClaw MCP server config under mcp.servers (default: false).

commands.plugins.label: Allow /plugins
commands.plugins.help: Allow /plugins chat command to list discovered plugins and toggle plugin enablement in config (default: false).

commands.debug.label: Allow /debug
commands.debug.help: Allow /debug chat command for runtime-only overrides (default: false).

commands.restart.label: Allow Restart
commands.restart.help: Allow /restart, /update, and external SIGUSR1 restart requests (default: true).

commands.ownerAllowFrom.label: Command Owners
commands.ownerAllowFrom.help: Explicit owner allowlist for owner-scoped commands. Use channel-native IDs (optionally prefixed like "whatsapp:+15551234567"). '*' is ignored.

commands.allowFrom.label: Command Elevated Access Rules
commands.allowFrom.help: Defines elevated command allow rules by channel and sender for owner-level command surfaces. Use narrow provider-specific identities so privileged commands are not exposed to broad chat audiences.

mcp.sessionIdleTtlMs.label: MCP Session Idle TTL (ms)
mcp.sessionIdleTtlMs.help: Optional idle eviction for OpenClaw session MCP runtimes in milliseconds. Unset or 0 keeps runtimes alive until session cleanup or Gateway shutdown. Positive values round down; active leases and pending acquisitions prevent eviction. Run-owned runtimes still retire when their one-shot run ends.

mcp.servers.label: MCP Servers
mcp.servers.help: Named MCP server definitions. OpenClaw stores them in its own config and runtime adapters decide which transports are supported at execution time.

mcp.servers.*.oauth.identity.label: MCP OAuth Identity
mcp.servers.*.oauth.identity.help: OAuth credential ownership for this server. Omit this field or use "shared" for operator-managed credentials; use "per-requester" to let each authenticated sender connect their own account.

mcp.servers.*.oauth.authProfileId.label: MCP OAuth Auth Profile
mcp.servers.*.oauth.authProfileId.help: Refresh-capable auth profile id used to inject the current bearer token into this remote MCP server. When set, OpenClaw resolves and refreshes the profile at runtime and does not project refresh material downstream.

mcp.servers.*.codex.label: Codex MCP Projection
mcp.servers.*.codex.help: OpenClaw projection metadata for Codex app-server threads only. It does not affect ACP sessions or generic Codex harness config. Omit this block to keep the server available to every Codex app-server agent with Codex's default MCP approval behavior.

mcp.servers.*.toolFilter.label: MCP Tool Selection
mcp.servers.*.toolFilter.help: Per-server MCP tool selection. Use include to expose only selected MCP tool names, or exclude to hide selected MCP tool names. Entries accept exact names and simple '*' globs.

mcp.servers.*.toolFilter.include.label: Included MCP Tools
mcp.servers.*.toolFilter.include.help: Exact MCP tool names or simple '*' globs to expose from this server. When omitted, all server tools remain eligible unless excluded.

mcp.servers.*.toolFilter.exclude.label: Excluded MCP Tools
mcp.servers.*.toolFilter.exclude.help: Exact MCP tool names or simple '*' globs to hide from this server.

mcp.servers.*.codex.agents.label: Codex MCP Agents
mcp.servers.*.codex.agents.help: Optional non-empty OpenClaw agent ids that should receive this MCP server in Codex app-server thread config. Empty, blank, or invalid lists fail closed; when omitted, the server is projected for all Codex app-server agents.

mcp.servers.*.codex.defaultToolsApproval.label: Codex MCP Tool Approval
mcp.servers.*.codex.defaultToolsApproval.help: Optional Codex MCP tool approval mode for this server: "auto", "prompt", or "approve". Use only for MCP servers you intentionally trust.

mcp.servers.*.codex.default_tools_approv.label: Codex MCP Tool Approval
mcp.servers.*.codex.default_tools_approv.help: Codex-native spelling for the same per-server MCP tool approval mode. Prefer defaultToolsApprovalMode in OpenClaw config.

ui.seamColor.label: Accent Color
ui.seamColor.help: Primary accent color used by UI surfaces for emphasis, badges, and visual identity cues. Use high-contrast values that remain readable across light/dark themes.

ui.prefs.accent.label: User Accent Color
ui.prefs.accent.help: User-selected Control UI accent color in #RRGGBB format. Overrides ui.seamColor; clear it to restore the configured seam color or theme default.

tui.label: Terminal UI
tui.help: Terminal UI display settings. Use this section for terminal-only presentation preferences without changing Gateway or other UI behavior.

tui.footer.label: Terminal UI Footer
tui.footer.help: Terminal UI footer display settings. Keep optional context compact so session, model, goal, and token information stay readable.

browser.evaluateEnabled.label: Browser Evaluate Enabled
browser.evaluateEnabled.help: Enables browser-side evaluate helpers for runtime script evaluation capabilities where supported. Keep disabled unless your workflows require evaluate semantics beyond snapshots/navigation.

browser.snapshotDefaults.label: Browser Snapshot Defaults
browser.snapshotDefaults.help: Default snapshot capture configuration used when callers do not provide explicit snapshot options. Tune this for consistent capture behavior across channels and automation paths.

browser.snapshotDefaults.mode.label: Browser Snapshot Mode
browser.snapshotDefaults.mode.help: Default snapshot extraction mode controlling how page content is transformed for agent consumption. Choose the mode that balances readability, fidelity, and token footprint for your workflows.

browser.tabCleanup.label: Browser Tab Cleanup
browser.tabCleanup.help: Best-effort cleanup policy for browser tabs opened by primary-agent sessions. Keep enabled to avoid stale sandbox or managed-browser tabs accumulating across long-lived gateways.

browser.tabCleanup.enabled.label: Browser Tab Cleanup Enabled
browser.tabCleanup.enabled.help: Enables cleanup of idle tracked browser tabs for primary-agent sessions. Disable only when external tooling owns tab lifecycle completely.

browser.ssrfPolicy.label: Browser SSRF Policy
browser.ssrfPolicy.help: Server-side request forgery guardrail settings for browser/network fetch paths that could reach internal hosts. Keep restrictive defaults in production and open only explicitly approved targets.

browser.ssrfPolicy.dangerouslyAllowPriva.label: Browser Dangerously Allow Private Network
browser.ssrfPolicy.dangerouslyAllowPriva.help: Allows access to private-network address ranges from browser tooling. Default is disabled when unset; enable only for explicitly trusted private-network destinations.

browser.ssrfPolicy.allowedHostnames.label: Browser Allowed Hostnames
browser.ssrfPolicy.allowedHostnames.help: Exact hostnames or IP literals allowed by browser SSRF policy checks. Keep the list minimal.

browser.ssrfPolicy.blockedHostnames.label: Browser Blocked Hostnames
browser.ssrfPolicy.blockedHostnames.help: Hostname patterns denied before DNS and allow rules, even with private-network access enabled. Supports exact hosts and "*.example.com" for subdomains only; add "example.com" separately to block the apex. Empty or unset adds no denials.

browser.ssrfPolicy.allowRfc2544Benchmark.label: Browser Allow RFC 2544 Benchmark Range
browser.ssrfPolicy.allowRfc2544Benchmark.help: Allow RFC 2544 benchmark-range IPs (198.18.0.0/15) for trusted fake-IP proxy environments.

browser.ssrfPolicy.allowIpv6UniqueLocalR.label: Browser Allow IPv6 Unique Local Range
browser.ssrfPolicy.allowIpv6UniqueLocalR.help: Allow IPv6 Unique Local Addresses (fc00::/7) for trusted fake-IP proxy environments.

session.scope.label: Session Scope
session.scope.help: Sets base session grouping strategy: "per-sender" isolates by sender and "global" shares one session per channel context. Keep "per-sender" for safer multi-user behavior unless deliberate shared context is required.

session.dmScope.label: DM Session Scope
session.dmScope.help: DM session scoping: "main" keeps continuity, while "per-peer", "per-channel-peer", and "per-account-channel-peer" increase isolation. Use isolated modes for shared inboxes or multi-account deployments.

session.groupScope.label: Group Session Scope
session.groupScope.help: Group/channel session scoping: "per-group" keeps rooms separate while the agent main session ambiently watches them, independently of dmScope; "main" merges room context into main and needs no watch. Use "main" only for trusted rooms.

session.identityLinks.label: Session Identity Links
session.identityLinks.help: Maps canonical identities to provider-prefixed peer IDs so equivalent users resolve to one DM thread (example: telegram:123456). Use this when the same human appears across multiple channels or accounts.

session.resetTriggers.label: Session Reset Triggers
session.resetTriggers.help: Lists message triggers that force a session reset when matched in inbound content. Use sparingly for explicit reset phrases so context is not dropped unexpectedly during normal conversation.

session.reset.label: Session Reset Policy
session.reset.help: Defines the default reset policy object used when no type-specific or channel-specific override applies. By default sessions do not reset automatically; use daily or idle schedules to opt in, while /new and /reset remain available at any time.

session.reset.mode.label: Session Reset Mode
session.reset.mode.help: Selects reset strategy: "none" disables automatic reset (the default), "daily" resets at a configured hour, and "idle" resets after inactivity. /new and /reset remain available in every mode.

session.reset.atHour.label: Session Daily Reset Hour
session.reset.atHour.help: Sets local-hour boundary (0-23) for daily reset mode so sessions roll over at predictable times. Use with mode=daily and align to operator timezone expectations for human-readable behavior.

session.reset.idleMinutes.label: Session Reset Idle Minutes
session.reset.idleMinutes.help: Sets inactivity window before reset for idle mode and can also act as secondary guard with daily mode. Use larger values to preserve continuity or smaller values for fresher short-lived threads.

session.resetByType.label: Session Reset by Chat Type
session.resetByType.help: Overrides reset behavior by chat type (direct, group, thread) when defaults are not sufficient. Use this when group/thread traffic needs different reset cadence than direct messages.

session.resetByType.direct.label: Session Reset (Direct)
session.resetByType.direct.help: Defines reset policy for direct chats and supersedes the base session.reset configuration for that type. Use this as the canonical direct-message override instead of the legacy dm alias.

session.resetByType.group.label: Session Reset (Group)
session.resetByType.group.help: Defines reset policy for group chat sessions where continuity and noise patterns differ from DMs. Use shorter idle windows for busy groups if context drift becomes a problem.

session.resetByType.thread.label: Session Reset (Thread)
session.resetByType.thread.help: Defines reset policy for thread-scoped sessions, including focused channel thread workflows. Use this when thread sessions should expire faster or slower than other chat types.

session.resetByChannel.label: Session Reset by Channel
session.resetByChannel.help: Provides channel-specific reset overrides keyed by provider/channel id for fine-grained behavior control. Use this only when one channel needs exceptional reset behavior beyond type-level policies.

session.store.label: Session Store Path
session.store.help: Sets the session storage file path used to persist session records across restarts. Use an explicit path only when you need custom disk layout, backup routing, or mounted-volume storage.

session.mainKey.label: Session Main Key
session.mainKey.help: Accepted but ignored: the per-agent main session suffix is always "main". Omit this field; global session scope uses "global" instead.

session.sendPolicy.label: Session Send Policy
session.sendPolicy.help: Controls cross-session send permissions using allow/deny rules evaluated against channel, chatType, and key prefixes. Use this to fence where session tools can deliver messages in complex environments.

session.sendPolicy.default.label: Session Send Policy Default Action
session.sendPolicy.default.help: Sets fallback action when no sendPolicy rule matches: "allow" or "deny". Keep "allow" for simpler setups, or choose "deny" when you require explicit allow rules for every destination.

session.sendPolicy.rules.label: Session Send Policy Rules
session.sendPolicy.rules.help: Ordered allow/deny rules evaluated before the default action, for example `{ action: "deny", match: { channel: "discord" } }`. Put most specific rules first so broad rules do not shadow exceptions.

session.sendPolicy.rules[].action.label: Session Send Rule Action
session.sendPolicy.rules[].action.help: Defines rule decision as "allow" or "deny" when the corresponding match criteria are satisfied. Use deny-first ordering when enforcing strict boundaries with explicit allow exceptions.

session.sendPolicy.rules[].match.label: Session Send Rule Match
session.sendPolicy.rules[].match.help: Defines optional rule match conditions that can combine channel, chatType, and key-prefix constraints. Keep matches narrow so policy intent stays readable and debugging remains straightforward.

session.sendPolicy.rules[].match.channel.label: Session Send Rule Channel
session.sendPolicy.rules[].match.channel.help: Matches rule application to a specific channel/provider id (for example discord, telegram, slack). Use this when one channel should permit or deny delivery independently of others.

session.sendPolicy.rules[].match.chatTyp.label: Session Send Rule Chat Type
session.sendPolicy.rules[].match.chatTyp.help: Matches rule application to chat type (direct, group, thread) so behavior varies by conversation form. Use this when DM and group destinations require different safety boundaries.

session.sendPolicy.rules[].match.keyPref.label: Session Send Rule Key Prefix
session.sendPolicy.rules[].match.keyPref.help: Matches a normalized session-key prefix after internal key normalization steps in policy consumers. Use this for general prefix controls, and prefer rawKeyPrefix when exact full-key matching is required.

session.sendPolicy.rules[].match.rawKeyP.label: Session Send Rule Raw Key Prefix
session.sendPolicy.rules[].match.rawKeyP.help: Matches the raw, unnormalized session-key prefix for exact full-key policy targeting. Use this when normalized keyPrefix is too broad and you need agent-prefixed or transport-specific precision.

session.threadBindings.label: Session Thread Bindings
session.threadBindings.help: Shared defaults for thread-bound session spawning and routing across supported channels. Configure global defaults here and override per channel only when behavior differs.

session.threadBindings.enabled.label: Thread Binding Enabled
session.threadBindings.enabled.help: Global master switch for thread-bound session spawning, routing, and delivery. Disable to turn off thread binding globally.

session.threadBindings.idleHours.label: Thread Binding Idle Timeout (hours)
session.threadBindings.idleHours.help: Default inactivity window in hours for thread-bound sessions across providers/channels (0 disables idle expiry). Default: 24.

session.threadBindings.maxAgeHours.label: Thread Binding Max Age (hours)
session.threadBindings.maxAgeHours.help: Optional hard max age in hours for thread-bound sessions across providers/channels (0 disables hard cap). Default: 0.

session.threadBindings.spawnSessions.label: Thread-Bound Session Spawns
session.threadBindings.spawnSessions.help: Global default gate for creating thread-bound work sessions from sessions_spawn and ACP thread spawns. Default: true when thread bindings are enabled.

session.threadBindings.defaultSpawnConte.label: Thread Spawn Context
session.threadBindings.defaultSpawnConte.help: Default native subagent context for thread-bound spawns. Use "fork" to start from the requester transcript or "isolated" for a clean child. Default: "fork".

session.sharing.label: Session Sharing Modes
session.sharing.help: Controls which collaboration modes session owners and administrators may select. Omitted booleans default to enabled; set a mode false to remove it from the picker and reject new selections.

session.sharing.readOnly.label: Allow Read-only Sessions
session.sharing.readOnly.help: Allows sessions to be made read-only for non-participants. Default: true.

session.sharing.suggest.label: Allow Suggest Sessions
session.sharing.suggest.help: Allows suggest visibility. In this phase it enforces the same admission policy as read-only; suggestion queues are configured by a later feature. Default: true.

session.sharing.drafts.label: Allow Draft Sessions
session.sharing.drafts.help: Allows draft visibility, which hides sessions from non-owner, non-admin operators. Default: true.

session.maintenance.label: Session Maintenance
session.maintenance.help: Automatic session-store maintenance controls for dashboard archiving, pruning age, entry caps, reset archive retention, and disk budget cleanup. Start in warn mode to observe impact, then enforce once thresholds are tuned.

session.maintenance.mode.label: Session Maintenance Mode
session.maintenance.mode.help: Determines whether maintenance policies are only reported ("warn") or actively applied ("enforce"). Keep "warn" during rollout and switch to "enforce" after validating safe thresholds.

session.maintenance.pruneAfter.label: Session Prune After
session.maintenance.pruneAfter.help: Archives eligible durable conversations and removes disposable automation entries older than this duration (default `30d`; for example `12h`). Archived conversations retain their history and can be restored; protected or routable conversations remain active.

session.maintenance.archiveDashboardAfte.label: Archive Inactive Dashboard Sessions After
session.maintenance.archiveDashboardAfte.help: Archives inactive dashboard sessions after this duration (for example `7d`) so they remain available without crowding the active session list. Set `false` or `0` to disable automatic dashboard archiving.

session.maintenance.maxEntries.label: Session Max Entries
session.maintenance.maxEntries.help: Caps unarchived session entries (default 5000). Eligible durable overflow conversations are archived with their history; disposable automation entries are removed. Existing archives do not consume the cap. Protected active entries still count and can keep the store above the limit.

session.maintenance.preserveRecent.label: Preserve Recent Sessions
session.maintenance.preserveRecent.help: Protects interactive sessions active within this duration (for example `7d`) from automatic age, count, and disk-budget history eviction. Unset or `false` keeps the normal oldest-first policy. Synthetic model-run, cron, hook, heartbeat, ACP, and sub-agent rows remain eligible for bounded cleanup.

session.maintenance.resetArchiveRetentio.label: Session Reset Archive Retention
session.maintenance.resetArchiveRetentio.help: Age-based retention for archived transcripts (`*.reset.<timestamp>` and `*.deleted.<timestamp>`). Defaults to keeping archives until the disk budget evicts them oldest-first; set a duration (for example `30d`) to opt into wall-clock deletion, or `false` to disable it explicitly.

session.maintenance.maxDiskBytes.label: Session Max Disk Budget
session.maintenance.maxDiskBytes.help: Per-agent physical disk budget covering SQLite main/WAL and counted session-directory artifacts (for example `500mb`). Defaults to `10gb`; protected data can keep usage above the target. When exceeded, warn mode reports pressure and enforce mode removes old reset/delete artifacts, unreferenced history, then cap-created archives. Manual, age-retention, dashboard, recovery, and legacy archives remain protected. Set `false`, `0`, or `"0"` to disable.

session.maintenance.highWaterBytes.label: Session Disk High-water Target
session.maintenance.highWaterBytes.help: Target size after disk-budget cleanup (high-water mark). Defaults to 80% of maxDiskBytes; set explicitly for tighter reclaim behavior on constrained disks. A value that resolves to zero falls back to the default; negative values are invalid. Disable the budget with maxDiskBytes instead.

cron.enabled.label: Automations Enabled
cron.enabled.help: Enables automation execution for stored schedules managed by the gateway. Keep enabled for normal reminder/automation flows, and disable only to pause all automation execution without deleting jobs.

cron.skipMissedJobs.label: Skip Missed Recurring Automations
cron.skipMissedJobs.help: Skips missed recurring cron/every slots at Gateway startup and schedules their next future occurrence instead of catching up. Default: false. Enable to avoid stale reminders after downtime; one-shot at jobs still catch up.

cron.webhookToken.label: Automations Webhook Bearer Token
cron.webhookToken.help: Bearer token attached to automation webhook POST deliveries when webhook mode is used. Prefer secret/env substitution and rotate this token regularly if shared webhook endpoints are internet-reachable.

cron.webhookSsrfPolicy.label: Automations Webhook SSRF Policy
cron.webhookSsrfPolicy.help: SSRF policy applied to every outbound automation webhook. Private, loopback, link-local, and internal targets stay blocked unless this policy explicitly allows them. Keep unset for strict delivery.

cron.webhookSsrfPolicy.dangerouslyAllowP.label: Automations Webhook Dangerously Allow Private Network
cron.webhookSsrfPolicy.dangerouslyAllowP.help: Allows automation webhooks to private and internal network targets. Keep disabled unless every configured webhook destination is trusted.

cron.webhookSsrfPolicy.allowedHostnames.label: Automations Webhook Allowed Hostnames
cron.webhookSsrfPolicy.allowedHostnames.help: Exact hostnames or IP literals allowed for automation webhook delivery, including otherwise blocked targets. Keep the list minimal.

cron.webhookSsrfPolicy.blockedHostnames.label: Automations Webhook Blocked Hostnames
cron.webhookSsrfPolicy.blockedHostnames.help: Hostname patterns denied before DNS and allow rules for automation webhook delivery. Supports exact hosts and "*.example.com" for subdomains only; add "example.com" separately to block the apex. Empty or unset adds no denials.

cron.webhookSsrfPolicy.allowRfc2544Bench.label: Automations Webhook Allow RFC 2544 Benchmark Range
cron.webhookSsrfPolicy.allowRfc2544Bench.help: Allows automation webhooks to RFC 2544 benchmark-range IPs (198.18.0.0/15). Use only with trusted fake-IP proxy environments.

cron.webhookSsrfPolicy.allowIpv6UniqueLo.label: Automations Webhook Allow IPv6 Unique Local Range
cron.webhookSsrfPolicy.allowIpv6UniqueLo.help: Allows automation webhooks to IPv6 Unique Local Addresses (fc00::/7). Use only with trusted fake-IP proxy environments.

cron.sessionRetention.label: Automations Session Retention
cron.sessionRetention.help: Controls how long completed automation run sessions are kept before pruning (`24h`, `7d`, `1h30m`, or `false` to disable pruning; a zero duration such as `0h` also disables; default: `24h`). Use shorter retention to reduce storage growth on high-frequency schedules.

transcripts.enabled.label: Transcripts Enabled
transcripts.enabled.help: Enables durable automatic meeting notes, the transcripts agent tool, and configured auto-start sources. Default: true. Set false to disable persistence and the tool; explicit meeting transcribe mode retains its bounded live tail.

transcripts.autoStart.label: Transcripts Auto-start Sources
transcripts.autoStart.help: Live transcript sources managed automatically from gateway startup. Each entry is enabled by being present; remove an entry to disable that source. Sources capture continuously unless whenOccupied is enabled.

transcripts.autoStart[].providerId.label: Transcript Source Provider ID
transcripts.autoStart[].providerId.help: Transcript source provider id, such as a Discord voice or future Slack huddle provider. Use the exact id exposed by the provider plugin.

transcripts.autoStart[].sessionId.label: Transcript Session ID
transcripts.autoStart[].sessionId.help: Optional fixed transcript session id for this auto-start source. Ignored when whenOccupied is true. Leave unset for generated ids unless you need a stable daily selector and can avoid same-day collisions.

transcripts.autoStart[].whenOccupied.label: Transcript Capture When Occupied
transcripts.autoStart[].whenOccupied.help: Start a fresh transcript session each time humans are present in the source and stop it (generating notes) after the last human leaves. Requires a provider that reports occupancy, such as discord-voice. Default: false (capture continuously from gateway start).

transcripts.autoStart[].title.label: Transcript Title
transcripts.autoStart[].title.help: Optional title for future transcript captures. Changing only titles keeps current captures running and does not rename their admitted title or saved notes. Other source changes retain their normal restart handling.

transcripts.autoStart[].accountId.label: Transcript Account ID
transcripts.autoStart[].accountId.help: Optional provider account or workspace identifier for transcript sources that need account disambiguation. Use the provider's documented account id format.

transcripts.autoStart[].guildId.label: Discord Guild ID
transcripts.autoStart[].guildId.help: Optional Discord guild id for Discord voice transcript sources. Configure this with the matching channelId when the provider needs guild-scoped voice channel lookup.

transcripts.autoStart[].channelId.label: Transcript Channel ID
transcripts.autoStart[].channelId.help: Provider channel id for the live transcript source, such as a Discord voice channel or Slack huddle channel. Verify provider-specific id semantics before enabling auto-start.

transcripts.autoStart[].meetingUrl.label: Transcript Meeting URL
transcripts.autoStart[].meetingUrl.help: Optional meeting URL for providers that join by URL instead of channel id. Use only trusted meeting links because auto-start may join and capture that meeting.

hooks.enabled.label: Hooks Enabled
hooks.enabled.help: Enables the hooks endpoint and mapping execution pipeline for inbound webhook requests. Keep disabled unless you are actively routing external events into the gateway.

hooks.path.label: Hooks Endpoint Path
hooks.path.help: HTTP path used by the hooks endpoint (for example `/hooks`) on the gateway control server. Use a non-guessable path and combine it with token validation for defense in depth.

hooks.token.label: Hooks Auth Token
hooks.token.help: Shared bearer token checked by hooks ingress for request authentication before mappings run. Treat holders as full-trust callers for the hook ingress surface, not as a separate non-owner role. Use environment substitution and rotate regularly when webhook endpoints are internet-accessible.

hooks.defaultSessionKey.label: Hooks Default Session Key
hooks.defaultSessionKey.help: Fallback session key used for hook deliveries when a request does not provide one through allowed channels. Use a stable but scoped key to avoid mixing unrelated automation conversations.

hooks.allowRequestSessionKey.label: Hooks Allow Request Session Key
hooks.allowRequestSessionKey.help: Allows callers to supply a session key in hook requests when true, enabling caller-controlled routing. Keep false unless trusted integrators explicitly need custom session threading.

hooks.allowedSessionKeyPrefixes.label: Hooks Allowed Session Key Prefixes
hooks.allowedSessionKeyPrefixes.help: Allowlist of accepted session-key prefixes for inbound hook requests when caller-provided keys are enabled. Use narrow prefixes to prevent arbitrary session-key injection.

hooks.allowedAgentIds.label: Hooks Allowed Agent IDs
hooks.allowedAgentIds.help: Allowlist of effective agent IDs that hook requests and mappings are allowed to target, including default-agent routing when agentId is omitted. Use this to constrain automation events to dedicated service agents and reduce blast radius if a hook token is exposed.

hooks.presets.label: Hooks Presets
hooks.presets.help: Named hook preset bundles applied at load time to seed standard mappings and behavior defaults. Keep preset usage explicit so operators can audit which automations are active.

hooks.transformsDir.label: Hooks Transforms Directory
hooks.transformsDir.help: Base directory for hook transform modules referenced by mapping transform.module paths. Use a controlled repo directory so dynamic imports remain reviewable and predictable.

hooks.mappings.label: Hook Mappings
hooks.mappings.help: Ordered mapping rules that match inbound hook requests and choose wake or agent actions with optional delivery routing. Use specific mappings first to avoid broad pattern rules capturing everything.

hooks.mappings[].id.label: Hook Mapping ID
hooks.mappings[].id.help: Optional stable identifier for a hook mapping entry used for auditing, troubleshooting, and targeted updates. Use unique IDs so logs and config diffs can reference mappings unambiguously.

hooks.mappings[].match.label: Hook Mapping Match
hooks.mappings[].match.help: Grouping object for mapping match predicates such as path and source before action routing is applied. Keep match criteria specific so unrelated webhook traffic does not trigger automations.

hooks.mappings[].match.path.label: Hook Mapping Match Path
hooks.mappings[].match.path.help: Path match condition for a hook mapping, usually compared against the inbound request path. Use this to split automation behavior by webhook endpoint path families.

hooks.mappings[].match.source.label: Hook Mapping Match Source
hooks.mappings[].match.source.help: Source match condition for a hook mapping, typically set by trusted upstream metadata or adapter logic. Use stable source identifiers so routing remains deterministic across retries.

hooks.mappings[].action.label: Hook Mapping Action
hooks.mappings[].action.help: Mapping action type: "wake" triggers agent wake flow, while "agent" sends directly to agent handling. Use "agent" for immediate execution and "wake" when heartbeat-driven processing is preferred.

hooks.mappings[].wakeMode.label: Hook Mapping Wake Mode
hooks.mappings[].wakeMode.help: Wake scheduling mode: "now" wakes immediately, while "next-heartbeat" defers until the next heartbeat cycle. Use deferred mode for lower-priority automations that can tolerate slight delay.

hooks.mappings[].name.label: Hook Mapping Name
hooks.mappings[].name.help: Human-readable mapping display name used in diagnostics and operator-facing config UIs. Keep names concise and descriptive so routing intent is obvious during incident review.

hooks.mappings[].agentId.label: Hook Mapping Agent ID
hooks.mappings[].agentId.help: Target agent ID for mapping execution when action routing should not use defaults. Use dedicated automation agents to isolate webhook behavior from interactive operator sessions.

hooks.mappings[].sessionKey.label: Hook Mapping Session Key
hooks.mappings[].sessionKey.help: Explicit session key override for mapping-delivered messages to control thread continuity. Use stable scoped keys so repeated events correlate without leaking into unrelated conversations.

hooks.mappings[].sessionMode.label: Hook Mapping Session Mode
hooks.mappings[].sessionMode.help: Controls mapping session continuity: "isolated" starts a fresh run session, while "persistent" reuses the resolved sessionKey. Keep isolated unless the integration intentionally needs durable context.

hooks.mappings[].messageTemplate.label: Hook Mapping Message Template
hooks.mappings[].messageTemplate.help: Template for synthesizing structured mapping input into the final message content sent to the target action path. Keep templates deterministic so downstream parsing and behavior remain stable.

hooks.mappings[].textTemplate.label: Hook Mapping Text Template
hooks.mappings[].textTemplate.help: Text-only fallback template used when rich payload rendering is not desired or not supported. Use this to provide a concise, consistent summary string for chat delivery surfaces.

hooks.mappings[].forEach.label: Hook Mapping Fan-Out Key
hooks.mappings[].forEach.help: Top-level payload array key the mapping fans out over: each element dispatches its own action, and templates or transforms see a payload whose array holds only the current element. The Gmail preset uses forEach: messages so batched pushes dispatch one run per email.

hooks.mappings[].deliver.label: Hook Mapping Deliver Reply
hooks.mappings[].deliver.help: Controls whether mapping execution results are delivered back to a channel destination versus being processed silently. Disable delivery for background automations that should not post user-facing output.

hooks.mappings[].allowUnsafeExternalCont.label: Hook Mapping Allow Unsafe External Content
hooks.mappings[].allowUnsafeExternalCont.help: When true, mapping content may include less-sanitized external payload data in generated messages. Keep false by default and enable only for trusted sources with reviewed transform logic.

hooks.mappings[].channel.label: Hook Mapping Delivery Channel
hooks.mappings[].channel.help: Delivery channel override for mapping outputs (for example "last", "telegram", "discord", "slack", "signal", "imessage", or "msteams"). Keep channel overrides explicit to avoid accidental cross-channel sends.

hooks.mappings[].to.label: Hook Mapping Delivery Destination
hooks.mappings[].to.help: Destination identifier inside the selected channel when mapping replies should route to a fixed target. Verify provider-specific destination formats before enabling production mappings.

hooks.mappings[].model.label: Hook Mapping Model Override
hooks.mappings[].model.help: Optional model override for mapping-triggered runs when automation should use a different model than agent defaults. Use this sparingly so behavior remains predictable across mapping executions.

hooks.mappings[].thinking.label: Hook Mapping Thinking Override
hooks.mappings[].thinking.help: Optional thinking-effort override for mapping-triggered runs to tune latency versus reasoning depth. Keep low or minimal for high-volume hooks unless deeper reasoning is clearly required.

hooks.mappings[].timeoutSeconds.label: Hook Mapping Timeout (sec)
hooks.mappings[].timeoutSeconds.help: Maximum runtime allowed for mapping action execution before timeout handling applies. Use tighter limits for high-volume webhook sources to prevent queue pileups.

hooks.mappings[].transform.label: Hook Mapping Transform
hooks.mappings[].transform.help: Transform configuration block defining module/export preprocessing before mapping action handling. Use transforms only from reviewed code paths and keep behavior deterministic for repeatable automation.

hooks.mappings[].transform.module.label: Hook Transform Module
hooks.mappings[].transform.module.help: Relative transform module path loaded from hooks.transformsDir to rewrite incoming payloads before delivery. Keep modules local, reviewed, and free of path traversal patterns.

hooks.mappings[].transform.export.label: Hook Transform Export
hooks.mappings[].transform.export.help: Named export to invoke from the transform module; defaults to module default export when omitted. Set this when one file hosts multiple transform handlers.

hooks.gmail.label: Gmail Hook
hooks.gmail.help: Gmail push integration settings used for Pub/Sub notifications and optional local callback serving. Keep this scoped to dedicated Gmail automation accounts where possible.

hooks.gmail.account.label: Gmail Hook Account
hooks.gmail.account.help: Google account identifier used for Gmail watch/subscription operations in this hook integration. Use a dedicated automation mailbox account to isolate operational permissions.

hooks.gmail.label.label: Gmail Hook Label
hooks.gmail.label.help: Optional Gmail label filter limiting which labeled messages trigger hook events. Keep filters narrow to avoid flooding automations with unrelated inbox traffic.

hooks.gmail.topic.label: Gmail Hook Pub/Sub Topic
hooks.gmail.topic.help: Google Pub/Sub topic name used by Gmail watch to publish change notifications for this account. Ensure the topic IAM grants Gmail publish access before enabling watches.

hooks.gmail.subscription.label: Gmail Hook Subscription
hooks.gmail.subscription.help: Pub/Sub subscription consumed by the gateway to receive Gmail change notifications from the configured topic. Keep subscription ownership clear so multiple consumers do not race unexpectedly.

hooks.gmail.pushToken.label: Gmail Hook Push Token
hooks.gmail.pushToken.help: Shared secret token required on Gmail push hook callbacks before processing notifications. Use env substitution and rotate if callback endpoints are exposed externally.

hooks.gmail.hookUrl.label: Gmail Hook Callback URL
hooks.gmail.hookUrl.help: Public callback URL Gmail or intermediaries invoke to deliver notifications into this hook pipeline. Keep this URL protected with token validation and restricted network exposure.

hooks.gmail.includeBody.label: Gmail Hook Include Body
hooks.gmail.includeBody.help: When true, fetch and include email body content for downstream mapping/agent processing. Keep false unless body text is required, because this increases payload size and sensitivity.

hooks.gmail.maxBytes.label: Gmail Hook Max Body Bytes
hooks.gmail.maxBytes.help: Maximum Gmail payload bytes processed per event when includeBody is enabled. Keep conservative limits to reduce oversized message processing cost and risk.

hooks.gmail.renewEveryMinutes.label: Gmail Hook Renew Interval (min)
hooks.gmail.renewEveryMinutes.help: Renewal cadence in minutes for Gmail watch subscriptions to prevent expiration. Set below provider expiration windows and monitor renew failures in logs.

hooks.gmail.allowUnsafeExternalContent.label: Gmail Hook Allow Unsafe External Content
hooks.gmail.allowUnsafeExternalContent.help: Allows less-sanitized external Gmail content to pass into processing when enabled. Keep disabled for safer defaults, and enable only for trusted mail streams with controlled transforms.

hooks.gmail.serve.label: Gmail Hook Local Server
hooks.gmail.serve.help: Local callback server settings block for directly receiving Gmail notifications without a separate ingress layer. Enable only when this process should terminate webhook traffic itself.

hooks.gmail.serve.bind.label: Gmail Hook Server Bind Address
hooks.gmail.serve.bind.help: Bind address for the local Gmail callback HTTP server used when serving hooks directly. Keep loopback-only unless external ingress is intentionally required.

hooks.gmail.serve.port.label: Gmail Hook Server Port
hooks.gmail.serve.port.help: Port for the local Gmail callback HTTP server when serve mode is enabled. Use a dedicated port to avoid collisions with gateway/control interfaces.

hooks.gmail.serve.path.label: Gmail Hook Server Path
hooks.gmail.serve.path.help: HTTP path on the local Gmail callback server where push notifications are accepted. Keep this consistent with subscription configuration to avoid dropped events.

hooks.gmail.tailscale.label: Gmail Hook Tailscale
hooks.gmail.tailscale.help: Tailscale exposure configuration block for publishing Gmail callbacks through Serve/Funnel routes. Use private tailnet modes before enabling any public ingress path.

hooks.gmail.tailscale.mode.label: Gmail Hook Tailscale Mode
hooks.gmail.tailscale.mode.help: Tailscale exposure mode for Gmail callbacks: "off", "serve", or "funnel". Use "serve" for private tailnet delivery and "funnel" only when public internet ingress is required.

hooks.gmail.tailscale.path.label: Gmail Hook Tailscale Path
hooks.gmail.tailscale.path.help: Path published by Tailscale Serve/Funnel for Gmail callback forwarding when enabled. Keep it aligned with Gmail webhook config so requests reach the expected handler.

hooks.gmail.tailscale.target.label: Gmail Hook Tailscale Target
hooks.gmail.tailscale.target.help: Local service target forwarded by Tailscale Serve/Funnel (for example http://127.0.0.1:8787). Use explicit loopback targets to avoid ambiguous routing.

hooks.gmail.model.label: Gmail Hook Model Override
hooks.gmail.model.help: Optional model override for Gmail-triggered runs when mailbox automations should use dedicated model behavior. Keep unset to inherit agent defaults unless mailbox tasks need specialization.

hooks.gmail.thinking.label: Gmail Hook Thinking Override
hooks.gmail.thinking.help: Thinking effort override for Gmail-driven agent runs: "off", "minimal", "low", "medium", or "high". Keep modest defaults for routine inbox automations to control cost and latency.

hooks.internal.label: Internal Hooks
hooks.internal.help: Internal hook runtime settings for bundled/custom event handlers loaded from module paths. Use this for trusted in-process automations and keep handler loading tightly scoped.

hooks.internal.enabled.label: Internal Hooks Enabled
hooks.internal.enabled.help: Enables processing for internal hooks and configured entries in the internal hook runtime. Keep disabled unless internal hooks are intentionally configured.

hooks.internal.entries.label: Internal Hook Entries
hooks.internal.entries.help: Configured internal hook entry records used to register concrete runtime handlers and metadata. Keep entries explicit and versioned so production behavior is auditable.

hooks.internal.load.label: Internal Hook Loader
hooks.internal.load.help: Internal hook loader settings controlling where handler modules are discovered at startup. Use constrained load roots to reduce accidental module conflicts or shadowing.

hooks.internal.load.extraDirs.label: Internal Hook Extra Directories
hooks.internal.load.extraDirs.help: Additional directories searched for internal hook modules beyond default load paths. Keep this minimal and controlled to reduce accidental module shadowing.

discovery.wideArea.label: Wide-area Discovery
discovery.wideArea.help: Wide-area discovery configuration group for exposing discovery signals beyond local-link scopes. Enable only in deployments that intentionally aggregate gateway presence across sites.

discovery.wideArea.domain.label: Wide-area Discovery Domain
discovery.wideArea.domain.help: Optional unicast DNS-SD domain for wide-area discovery, such as openclaw.internal. Use this when you intentionally publish gateway discovery beyond local mDNS scopes.

discovery.mdns.label: mDNS Discovery
discovery.mdns.help: mDNS discovery configuration group for local network advertisement and discovery behavior tuning. Keep minimal mode for routine LAN discovery unless extra metadata is required.

talk.agentId.label: Talk Agent
talk.agentId.help: Agent that owns Talk sessions created without an explicit agent-scoped session key.

talk.speechLocale.label: Talk Speech Locale
talk.speechLocale.help: BCP 47 locale id for Talk speech recognition on device nodes and the iOS system-voice fallback, for example "ru-RU". Leave unset to use each device default.

talk.interruptOnSpeech.label: Talk Interrupt on Speech
talk.interruptOnSpeech.help: If true (default), stop assistant speech when the user starts speaking in Talk mode. Keep enabled for conversational turn-taking.

talk.silenceTimeoutMs.label: Talk Silence Timeout (ms)
talk.silenceTimeoutMs.help: Milliseconds of user silence before Talk mode finalizes and sends the current transcript. Leave unset to keep the platform default pause window (700 ms on macOS and Android, 900 ms on iOS).

talk.consultThinkingLevel.label: Talk Consult Thinking Level
talk.consultThinkingLevel.help: Use this to override the thinking level for the regular agent run behind Talk realtime consults.

talk.consultFastMode.label: Talk Consult Fast Mode
talk.consultFastMode.help: Use this to set true or false fast mode for the regular agent run behind Talk realtime consults.

messages.visibleReplies.label: Visible Replies
messages.visibleReplies.help: Controls model-authored source replies across direct, group, and channel conversations. "message_tool" requires message(action=send) for normal assistant output and generic tool media; explicitly host-owned runtime output remains deliverable except for ambient room events. "automatic" posts normal replies as before.

messages.usageTemplate.label: Usage Footer Template
messages.usageTemplate.help: Custom /usage full footer template, either an inline object or a JSON file path. Invalid or unavailable templates fall back to the built-in usage line.

messages.responseUsage.label: Default Usage Footer Mode
messages.responseUsage.help: Default per-reply usage footer mode ("off"|"tokens"|"full") seeded into sessions that have not chosen one via /usage. Also accepts "on" as a legacy alias for "tokens". Accepts a bare mode or a per-channel map with a "default" fallback. Precedence: session value -> channel entry -> default -> off; an explicit /usage choice (including off) is persisted and overrides the default. Use /usage reset (aliases: inherit, clear, default) to clear a session override and re-inherit this configured default.

messages.groupChat.label: Group Chat Rules
messages.groupChat.help: Group-message handling controls including mention triggers and history window sizing. Keep mention patterns narrow so group channels do not trigger on every message.

messages.groupChat.mentionPatterns.label: Group Mention Patterns
messages.groupChat.mentionPatterns.help: Safe case-insensitive regex patterns used to detect explicit mentions/trigger phrases in group chats. Use precise patterns to reduce false positives in high-volume channels; invalid or unsafe nested-repetition patterns are ignored.

messages.groupChat.historyLimit.label: Group History Limit
messages.groupChat.historyLimit.help: Maximum number of prior group messages loaded as context per turn for group sessions. Use higher values for richer continuity, or lower values for faster and cheaper responses.

messages.groupChat.unmentionedInbound.label: Group Unmentioned Inbound
messages.groupChat.unmentionedInbound.help: Controls how unmentioned always-on group chatter is submitted. "user_request" treats it as a user request; "room_event" submits it as quiet context where visible output requires the message tool.

messages.groupChat.visibleReplies.label: Group Visible Replies
messages.groupChat.visibleReplies.help: Overrides model-authored source replies for group/channel conversations. Defaults to "automatic" when no global visible reply policy is set. "message_tool" requires message(action=send) for normal assistant output and generic tool media; explicitly host-owned runtime output remains deliverable except for ambient room events. "automatic" posts normal replies as before.

messages.queue.label: Inbound Queue
messages.queue.help: Queue strategy for inbound messages that arrive while a session run is active. Use this to tune steering, deferred followups, batching, or interruption.

messages.queue.mode.label: Queue Mode
messages.queue.mode.help: Queue mode for active runs. Use "steer" to inject prompts into the active run, "followup" to run later, "collect" to batch compatible messages later, or "interrupt" to abort the active run before starting the newest prompt.

messages.queue.byChannel.label: Queue Mode by Channel
messages.queue.byChannel.help: Per-channel queue mode overrides keyed by provider id (for example telegram, discord, slack). Use this when one channel's traffic pattern needs different behavior than global defaults.

messages.queue.debounceMsByChannel.label: Queue Fallback Debounce by Channel (ms)
messages.queue.debounceMsByChannel.help: Per-channel debounce overrides for queue behavior keyed by provider id. Use this to tune burst handling independently for chat surfaces with different pacing.

messages.queue.cap.label: Queue Capacity
messages.queue.cap.help: Maximum number of queued inbound items retained before drop policy applies. Default is 20; keep caps bounded in noisy channels so memory usage remains predictable.

messages.queue.drop.label: Queue Drop Strategy
messages.queue.drop.help: Drop strategy when queue cap is exceeded. "summarize" drops oldest entries but preserves compact summaries; "old" drops oldest without summaries; "new" rejects the newest item. Use "summarize" for long-running chats where context matters.

messages.inbound.label: Inbound Debounce
messages.inbound.help: Direct inbound debounce settings used before queue/turn processing starts. Configure this for provider-specific rapid message bursts from the same sender.

messages.ackReaction.label: Ack Reaction Emoji
messages.ackReaction.help: Emoji reaction used to acknowledge inbound messages (empty disables).

messages.ackReactionScope.label: Ack Reaction Scope
messages.ackReactionScope.help: When to send ack reactions ("group-mentions", "group-all", "direct", "all", "off", "none"). "group-mentions" acks group messages that mention the agent, whether or not the group requires mentions; "group-all" acks every group message. "off"/"none" disables ack reactions entirely.

messages.statusReactions.label: Status Reactions
messages.statusReactions.help: Lifecycle status reactions that update the emoji on the trigger message as the agent progresses (queued → thinking → tool → done/error).

messages.statusReactions.enabled.label: Enable Status Reactions
messages.statusReactions.enabled.help: Enable lifecycle status reactions on supported channels. Discord treats unset as enabled when ack reactions are active; Slack, Signal, Telegram, and WhatsApp require this to be true before lifecycle reactions are used. Slack uses native assistant thread status for progress by default.

messages.inbound.debounceMs.label: Inbound Message Debounce (ms)
messages.inbound.debounceMs.help: Debounce window (ms) for batching rapid inbound messages from the same sender (0 to disable).

messages.inbound.byChannel.label: Inbound Debounce by Channel (ms)
messages.inbound.byChannel.help: Per-channel inbound debounce overrides keyed by provider id in milliseconds. Use this where some providers send message fragments more aggressively than others.

tts.persona.label: TTS Persona
tts.persona.help: Default TTS persona id. Local TTS persona preferences can override this per host.

tts.personas.label: TTS Personas
tts.personas.help: Named TTS personas that define stable spoken identity plus provider-specific speech bindings.

tts.personas.*.label: TTS Persona
tts.personas.*.help: One TTS persona. Use provider-specific bindings for exact voices/models and prompt templates.

tts.personas.*.providers.label: TTS Persona Provider Bindings
tts.personas.*.providers.help: Provider-specific TTS persona bindings keyed by speech provider id. These merge over tts.providers for the active persona.

tts.providers.label: TTS Provider Settings
tts.providers.help: Provider-specific TTS settings keyed by speech provider id. Use this instead of bundled provider-specific top-level keys so speech plugins stay decoupled from core config schema.

tts.providers.*.label: TTS Provider Config
tts.providers.*.help: Provider-specific TTS configuration for one speech provider id. Keep fields scoped to the plugin that owns that provider.

tts.providers.*.apiKey.label: TTS Provider API Key
tts.providers.*.apiKey.help: Provider API key used by that speech provider when its plugin requires authenticated TTS access.

talk.providers.label: Talk Provider Settings
talk.providers.help: Provider-specific Talk settings keyed by provider id. During migration, prefer this over legacy talk.* keys.

talk.providers.*.label: Talk Provider Config
talk.providers.*.help: Provider-owned Talk config fields for the matching provider id.

talk.providers.*.apiKey.label: Talk Provider API Key
talk.providers.*.apiKey.help: Provider API key for Talk mode.

talk.realtime.label: Talk Realtime
talk.realtime.help: Realtime Talk provider, model, voice, mode, transport, and brain strategy. Keep speech/TTS provider config in talk.provider and talk.providers.

talk.realtime.provider.label: Talk Realtime Provider
talk.realtime.provider.help: Active realtime voice provider id, such as openai or google.

talk.realtime.providers.label: Talk Realtime Provider Settings
talk.realtime.providers.help: Provider-specific realtime voice settings keyed by provider id.

talk.realtime.providers.*.label: Talk Realtime Provider Config
talk.realtime.providers.*.help: Provider-owned realtime voice config for the matching provider id.

talk.realtime.providers.*.apiKey.label: Talk Realtime Provider API Key
talk.realtime.providers.*.apiKey.help: Provider API key for realtime Talk.

talk.realtime.model.label: Talk Realtime Model
talk.realtime.model.help: Realtime provider model id override for browser or Gateway-owned Talk sessions.

talk.realtime.speakerVoice.label: Talk Realtime Speaker Voice
talk.realtime.speakerVoice.help: Realtime provider speaker voice name override for browser or Gateway-owned Talk sessions.

talk.realtime.speakerVoiceId.label: Talk Realtime Speaker Voice ID
talk.realtime.speakerVoiceId.help: Realtime provider speaker voice id override for browser or Gateway-owned Talk sessions.

talk.realtime.instructions.label: Talk Realtime Instructions
talk.realtime.instructions.help: Additional system instructions appended to OpenClaw's built-in realtime Talk prompt. Use this for voice style, tone, and other provider-facing realtime behavior while keeping agent-consult guidance intact.

talk.realtime.mode.label: Talk Realtime Mode
talk.realtime.mode.help: Talk execution mode: realtime, stt-tts, or transcription.

talk.realtime.transport.label: Talk Realtime Transport
talk.realtime.transport.help: Talk byte/session transport: webrtc, provider-websocket, gateway-relay, or managed-room.

talk.realtime.vadThreshold.label: Talk Realtime VAD Threshold
talk.realtime.vadThreshold.help: Realtime voice activity detection threshold from 0 (most sensitive) to 1 (least sensitive).

talk.realtime.silenceDurationMs.label: Talk Realtime Silence Duration (ms)
talk.realtime.silenceDurationMs.help: Milliseconds of silence before a realtime Talk user turn is committed.

talk.realtime.prefixPaddingMs.label: Talk Realtime Prefix Padding (ms)
talk.realtime.prefixPaddingMs.help: Milliseconds of audio retained before realtime voice activity is detected.

talk.realtime.reasoningEffort.label: Talk Realtime Reasoning Effort
talk.realtime.reasoningEffort.help: Provider-specific reasoning effort for realtime Talk sessions, such as minimal, low, medium, or high.

talk.realtime.brain.label: Talk Realtime Brain
talk.realtime.brain.help: Talk reasoning strategy: agent-consult for Gateway-mediated agent help, direct-tools for local tool calls, or none.

talk.realtime.consultRouting.label: Talk Realtime Consult Routing
talk.realtime.consultRouting.help: Gateway relay fallback for final user transcripts when the realtime provider skips openclaw_agent_consult. provider-direct preserves provider replies; force-agent-consult routes through OpenClaw.

channels.defaults.label: Channel Defaults
channels.defaults.help: Default channel behavior applied across providers when provider-specific settings are not set. Use this to enforce consistent baseline policy before per-provider tuning.

channels.defaults.groupPolicy.label: Default Group Policy
channels.defaults.groupPolicy.help: Default group policy across channels: "open", "disabled", or "allowlist". Keep "allowlist" for safer production setups unless broad group participation is intentional.

channels.defaults.contextVisibility.label: Default Context Visibility
channels.defaults.contextVisibility.help: Default supplemental context visibility for fetched quote/thread/history content: "all" (keep all context), "allowlist" (only allowlisted senders), or "allowlist_quote" (allowlist + keep explicit quotes).

channels.defaults.implicitMentions.label: Default Implicit Mentions
channels.defaults.implicitMentions.help: Default policy for whether reply-to-bot, quoted-bot, and bot-participated-thread facts activate supporting message channels without an explicit mention.

channels.defaults.implicitMentions.reply.label: Default Reply-to-Bot Implicit Mentions
channels.defaults.implicitMentions.reply.help: Treat replies to the bot's own messages as implicit mentions by default. Defaults to true for backward compatibility.

channels.defaults.implicitMentions.quote.label: Default Quoted-Bot Implicit Mentions
channels.defaults.implicitMentions.quote.help: Treat quoted bot messages as implicit mentions by default. Defaults to true for backward compatibility.

channels.defaults.implicitMentions.threa.label: Default Thread-Participation Implicit Mentions
channels.defaults.implicitMentions.threa.help: Treat follow-ups in threads where the bot participated as implicit mentions by default. Defaults to true for backward compatibility.

channels.defaults.heartbeatVisibility.label: Default Heartbeat Visibility
channels.defaults.heartbeatVisibility.help: Default heartbeat visibility settings for status messages emitted by providers/channels. Tune this globally to reduce noisy healthy-state updates while keeping alerts visible.

channels.defaults.heartbeatVisibility.sh.label: Heartbeat Show OK
channels.defaults.heartbeatVisibility.sh.help: Shows healthy/OK heartbeat status entries when true in channel status outputs. Keep false in noisy environments and enable only when operators need explicit healthy confirmations.

channels.defaults.heartbeatVisibility.sh.label: Heartbeat Show Alerts
channels.defaults.heartbeatVisibility.sh.help: Shows degraded/error heartbeat alerts when true so operator channels surface problems promptly. Keep enabled in production so broken channel states are visible.

channels.defaults.heartbeatVisibility.us.label: Heartbeat Use Indicator
channels.defaults.heartbeatVisibility.us.help: Enables concise indicator-style heartbeat rendering instead of verbose status text where supported. Use indicator mode for dense dashboards with many active channels.

channels.defaults.botLoopProtection.label: Default Bot Loop Protection
channels.defaults.botLoopProtection.help: Default pair loop protection settings for channel providers that support bot-to-bot loop guards. Use provider-specific overrides only when one channel needs a different budget.

channels.defaults.botLoopProtection.enab.label: Default Bot Loop Protection Enabled
channels.defaults.botLoopProtection.enab.help: Enables pair loop protection by default for supporting channels when bot-authored messages can reach dispatch. Providers may still disable the guard when bots are ignored.

channels.defaults.botLoopProtection.maxE.label: Default Bot Loop Events per Window
channels.defaults.botLoopProtection.maxE.help: Maximum events a sender/receiver pair may exchange within the configured window before suppression starts. Default for supporting channels is 20.

channels.defaults.botLoopProtection.wind.label: Default Bot Loop Window Seconds
channels.defaults.botLoopProtection.wind.help: Sliding window length in seconds for pair loop budgets. Default for supporting channels is 60.

channels.defaults.botLoopProtection.cool.label: Default Bot Loop Cooldown Seconds
channels.defaults.botLoopProtection.cool.help: Cooldown seconds applied to a pair after it exceeds the loop budget. Default for supporting channels is 60.

channels.modelByChannel.label: Channel Model Overrides
channels.modelByChannel.help: Map provider -> channel id / DM peer id -> model override (values are provider/model or aliases).

discovery.mdns.mode.label: mDNS Discovery Mode
discovery.mdns.mode.help: mDNS broadcast mode ("minimal" default, "full" includes cliPath/sshPort, "off" disables mDNS).

plugins.enabled.label: Enable Plugins
plugins.enabled.help: Enable or disable plugin/extension loading globally during startup and config reload (default: true). Keep enabled only when extension capabilities are required by your deployment.

plugins.allow.label: Plugin Allowlist
plugins.allow.help: Optional allowlist of plugin IDs; when set, only listed plugins are eligible to load. Configured bundled chat channels can still activate their bundled plugin when the channel is explicitly enabled in config. Use this to enforce approved extension inventories in controlled environments.

plugins.deny.label: Plugin Denylist
plugins.deny.help: Optional denylist of plugin IDs that are blocked even if allowlists or paths include them. Use deny rules for emergency rollback and hard blocks on risky plugins.

plugins.load.label: Plugin Loader
plugins.load.help: Plugin loader configuration group for specifying filesystem paths where plugins are discovered. Keep load paths explicit and reviewed to avoid accidental untrusted extension loading.

plugins.load.paths.label: Plugin Load Paths
plugins.load.paths.help: Additional plugin files or directories scanned by the loader beyond built-in defaults. Use dedicated extension directories and avoid broad paths with unrelated executable content.

plugins.slots.label: Plugin Slots
plugins.slots.help: Selects which plugins own exclusive runtime slots such as memory so only one plugin provides that capability. Use explicit slot ownership to avoid overlapping providers with conflicting behavior.

plugins.slots.memory.label: Memory Plugin
plugins.slots.memory.help: Select the active memory plugin by id, or "none" to disable memory plugins.

plugins.slots.contextEngine.label: Context Engine Plugin
plugins.slots.contextEngine.help: Selects the active context engine plugin by id so one plugin provides context orchestration behavior.

plugins.entries.label: Plugin Entries
plugins.entries.help: Per-plugin settings keyed by plugin ID including enablement and plugin-specific runtime configuration payloads. Use this for scoped plugin tuning without changing global loader policy.

plugins.entries.*.enabled.label: Plugin Enabled
plugins.entries.*.enabled.help: Per-plugin enablement override for a specific entry, applied on top of global plugin policy. With the default hybrid reload mode, changes hot-reload the plugin runtime for new agent turns without restarting the Gateway unless the plugin requires a restart for this path. Use this to stage plugin rollout gradually across environments.

plugins.entries.*.hooks.label: Plugin Hook Policy
plugins.entries.*.hooks.help: Per-plugin typed hook policy controls for core-enforced safety gates. Use this to constrain high-impact hook categories without disabling the entire plugin.

plugins.entries.*.hooks.allowConversatio.label: Allow Conversation Access Hooks
plugins.entries.*.hooks.allowConversatio.help: Controls whether this plugin may read raw conversation content from typed hooks such as `before_agent_run`, `before_model_resolve`, `before_agent_reply`, `llm_input`, `llm_output`, `before_agent_finalize`, and `agent_end`. Non-bundled plugins must opt in explicitly.

plugins.entries.*.hooks.allowPromptInjec.label: Allow Prompt Injection Hooks
plugins.entries.*.hooks.allowPromptInjec.help: Controls whether this plugin may mutate prompts through typed hooks. Set false to block `before_prompt_build`.

plugins.entries.*.hooks.timeoutMs.label: Plugin Hook Timeout (ms)
plugins.entries.*.hooks.timeoutMs.help: Default timeout in milliseconds for this plugin's typed hooks, capped at 600000. Use this to bound slow plugin hooks without changing plugin code; per-hook values in hooks.timeouts take precedence.

plugins.entries.*.hooks.timeouts.label: Plugin Hook Timeout Overrides
plugins.entries.*.hooks.timeouts.help: Per-hook timeout overrides in milliseconds keyed by typed hook name, capped at 600000. Use narrow overrides for known slow hooks such as before_prompt_build or agent_end instead of raising every hook timeout.

plugins.entries.*.subagent.label: Plugin Subagent Policy
plugins.entries.*.subagent.help: Per-plugin subagent runtime controls for model override trust and allowlists. Keep this unset unless a plugin must explicitly steer subagent model selection.

plugins.entries.*.subagent.allowModelOve.label: Allow Plugin Subagent Model Override
plugins.entries.*.subagent.allowModelOve.help: Explicitly allows this plugin to request provider/model overrides in background subagent runs. Keep false unless the plugin is trusted to steer model selection.

plugins.entries.*.subagent.allowedModels.label: Plugin Subagent Allowed Models
plugins.entries.*.subagent.allowedModels.help: Allowed override targets for trusted plugin subagent runs as canonical "provider/model" refs. Use "*" only when you intentionally allow any model.

plugins.entries.*.llm.label: Plugin LLM Policy
plugins.entries.*.llm.help: Per-plugin api.runtime.llm.complete controls for model and agent override trust. Keep this unset unless a plugin must explicitly steer host-owned completion calls.

plugins.entries.*.llm.allowModelOverride.label: Allow Plugin LLM Model Override
plugins.entries.*.llm.allowModelOverride.help: Explicitly allows this plugin to request model overrides in api.runtime.llm.complete. Keep false unless the plugin is trusted to steer model selection.

plugins.entries.*.llm.allowedModels.label: Plugin LLM Allowed Models
plugins.entries.*.llm.allowedModels.help: Allowed override targets for trusted plugin LLM calls as canonical "provider/model" refs. Use "*" only when you intentionally allow any model override.

plugins.entries.*.llm.allowedCompletionM.label: Plugin LLM Allowed Completion Models
plugins.entries.*.llm.allowedCompletionM.help: Allowed targets for every plugin LLM completion as canonical "provider/model" refs, including host-resolved defaults and overrides. Use "*" only when you intentionally allow any model.

plugins.entries.*.llm.allowAuthProfileOv.label: Allow Plugin LLM Auth Profile Override
plugins.entries.*.llm.allowAuthProfileOv.help: Allows this plugin to select a non-default auth profile for isolated agent-runtime completions. Keep false unless the plugin is trusted for explicit isolated credential routing.

plugins.entries.*.llm.allowAgentIdOverri.label: Allow Plugin LLM Agent Override
plugins.entries.*.llm.allowAgentIdOverri.help: Explicitly allows this plugin to request api.runtime.llm.complete against a non-default agent id. Keep false unless the plugin is trusted for cross-agent model access.

plugins.entries.*.apiKey.label: Plugin API Key
plugins.entries.*.apiKey.help: Optional API key field consumed by plugins that accept direct key configuration in entry settings. Use secret/env substitution and avoid committing real credentials into config files.

plugins.entries.*.env.label: Plugin Environment Variables
plugins.entries.*.env.help: Per-plugin environment variable map injected for that plugin runtime context only. Use this to scope provider credentials to one plugin instead of sharing global process environment.

plugins.entries.*.config.label: Plugin Config
plugins.entries.*.config.help: Plugin-defined configuration payload interpreted by that plugin's own schema and validation rules. Use only documented fields from the plugin to prevent ignored or invalid settings.
